title: Expert Perspectives on Transparency and Trust in AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems for Chest X-Ray Diagnosis: Qualitative Study.
abstract: Background The integration of AI-based Clinical Decision Support Systems (AI-CDSS) into clinical practice has expanded rapidly, particularly in medical imaging. Beyond algorithmic performance, growing evidence suggests that clinicians' engagement with AI-CDSS is shaped by how transparently systems communicate their outputs, and how trust is formed through human-AI interaction. However, a limited understanding of how these concepts are perceived by end users and developers continues to hinder real-world implementation. Objective This study aims to explore expert perspectives on transparency and trust in AI-CDSS for chest X-ray diagnosis, with a focus on the two-dimensional lens: user interface and users' mental models. Methods A qualitative study was conducted using semistructured interviews with a total of 21 experts, including 11 radiologists and 10 AI experts experienced in AI-CDSS. Data were analyzed thematically to explore factors perceived to influence transparent communication and trust. Results Three themes emerged: (1) perspective of transparency and trust, (2) user interface, and (3) users' mental models. Findings reveal that trust is a dynamic calibration process developed through repeated use, feedback loops, and alignment with clinicians' mental models, rather than algorithmic accuracy alone. Significant discrepancies were identified between how developers design system transparency and how clinicians interpret AI outputs. Conclusions This study demonstrates that transparency and trust are achieved through interpretable outputs, clear communication of system limitations, and alignment with clinical workflows. Designing trustworthy AI-CDSS requires integrating transparent interface design with consideration of users' knowledge, experience, and attitudes to support effective human-AI interaction.

title: Patient-Specific Virtual Reality for Lumbar Decompression Surgery: An Automated Imaging Pipeline and Educational Assessment
abstract: Manual construction of patient-specific models has limited the use of virtual reality (VR) for case-specific spine surgical rehearsal, and simulator assessments are often not patient-specific. We present a largely automated pipeline that converts routine preoperative CT and MRI into patient-specific 3D models for VR rehearsal of lumbar decompression, paired with case-specific written assessments. CT was segmented with an unmodified vertebral network and MRI with an in-house nnU-Net; volumes were registered and exported for VR. A locally hosted large language model generated per-case assessments from each patient's radiology report; the pipeline ran in approximately two minutes per case, and MRI segmentation reached a mean Dice of 0.870. Eight patient-specific models were prepared, and eleven trainees (undergraduate to fellow) completed a faculty-guided session with pre/post knowledge testing. Knowledge scores increased from 5.82 to 7.27 out of 10 (Wilcoxon $p=0.008$; Cohen's $d=1.01$), with 8 of 11 improving and none declining, and trainees rated educational value favorably. This feasibility study demonstrates a fast, fully private pipeline producing patient-specific VR models and matched assessments; the educational findings are preliminary and uncontrolled, motivating a larger controlled trial.

title: Feasibility of Augmented Reality-Guided Robotic Ultrasound with Cone-Beam CT Integration for Spine Procedures
abstract: Needle placement in spine interventions is critical for effective pain management, yet it depends on reliable identification of anatomical landmarks and careful trajectory planning. Conventional imaging guidance often relies on both computed tomography (CT) and X-ray fluoroscopy, exposing patients and staff to high doses of radiation while providing limited real-time 3D feedback. The choice of visualization may also affect operator performance and cognitive workload. We present an optical see-through augmented reality (OST-AR)–guided robotic system for spine procedures that provides in situ visualization of spinal structures to support needle trajectory planning. We integrate a cone-beam CT (CBCT)-derived 3D spine model, which is co-registered with live ultrasound, enabling users to combine global anatomical context with local, real-time imaging. We evaluated the system in a phantom user study involving two representative spine procedures: facet joint injection and lumbar puncture. Sixteen participants performed insertions under two visualization conditions: conventional screen vs. AR. Results show that AR significantly reduces execution time and across-task placement error, while also improving usability, trust, and spatial understanding, and lowering cognitive workload. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of AR-guided robotic ultrasound for spine interventions, highlighting its potential to enhance accuracy, efficiency, and user experience in image-guided procedures.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of SAM3 for Left Atrium Segmentation from MR Images for Improved Planning and Guidance of Cardiac Ablation Interventions
abstract: Foundation models such as Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) have demonstrated strong generalization in natural images through prompt-driven segmentation. However, their applicability to medical imaging remains unclear due to the domain-specific visual characteristics and task requirements. In this work, we investigate the domain adaptability of SAM3 for left atrium (LA) segmentation from cardiac MRI, a challenging, yet clinically critical task in the context of image-guided cardiac interventions, specifically aimed at improving planning and guidance of catheter-based cardiac ablation therapy in arrhythmia patients. We first evaluate SAM3 in a zero-shot setting using text prompts and show that performance remains limited despite descriptive prompt formulations, highlighting a fundamental mismatch between semantic prompting and the visual cues required for medical image segmentation. To address this limitation, we study two parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies, including LoRA and a prompt-free adapter-based framework. Our comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that LoRA achieves stronger performance (Dice 90.6% and 91.7%) over zero-shot baselines and cross-dataset generalization. LoRA leverages the semantic priors, while the adapter provides stable predictions with improved computational efficiency. In particular, adapter training reduces per-epoch training time by over 7× compared to LoRA, while maintaining comparable segmentation performance. These findings reveal a key trade-off between generalization and efficiency and show that semantic guidance from text prompts and feature-level adaptation to modality-specific visual cues offer two viable, complementary pathways for adapting SAM3 to cardiac MRI. Our code is available here.

title: Pan-cancer ctDNA panel and PET/CT in predicting true disease status after curative-intent treatment of head and neck cancer: a preliminary study.
abstract: Background and purpose Early detection of minimal residual disease is essential in managing head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), and positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) has been the standard imaging modality. Liquid biopsy (LB) of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has been introduced as a complementary method to enhance its diagnostic performance. The study aimed to investigate the performance of a pan-cancer ctDNA panel in conjunction with conventional PET/CT in the treatment response assessment. Patient/material and methods: Thirty-four patients with newly diagnosed HNSCC were prospectively enrolled, and 17 patients completed the study protocol. All patients underwent standard [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging and a single timepoint LB 3 months after completion of definitive oncological treatment. A commercially available pan-cancer assay was utilized for ctDNA detection and tissue genomic analysis. Statistical assessments were performed separately for pathogenic variants of ctDNA detected concordantly in tissue and LB and for all detected pathogenic variants of ctDNA. Results The combination of ctDNA detection of concordant variants and PET/CT imaging contributed to the highest diagnostic accuracy in predicting true disease status. Sensitivity was highest for the combination of ctDNA detection of all variants and PET/CT imaging. Recurrence-free and overall survival were higher in patients having a negative LB in assessments of concordant variants when compared to those with a positive LB (p < 0.001 for both). Interpretation A single-timepoint ctDNA detection with pan-cancer assay combined with PET/CT appears as a promising method for predicting true disease status in HNSCC. Our findings are presented as hypothesis generating due to the limited sample size.

title: Prevalence and morphological types of middle mesial canals in mandibular molars according to the Barros-Costa classification: a CBCT study in a Turkish subpopulation.
abstract: Objective The purpose of this study was to assess the prevalence and configurations of middle mesial canals (MMCs) in a Turkish subpopulation using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) according to the Barros-Costa classification. Materials and methods Two experienced endodontists assessed the prevalence of MMCs in mandibular molars of 213 Turkish patients aged 18-65 years (111 females, 102 males). MMCs were categorized using the Barros-Costa classification based on their association with the mesiobuccal and mesiolingual canals using CBCT scans in all three planes. Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests were used for unadjusted comparisons (p < 0.05). A multivariable generalized estimating equations (GEE) model with patient ID as the clustering variable was used to assess the associations between MMC presence and tooth type, age, and sex. Results Of 589 mandibular molars evaluated, 12.4% had an MMC. Distribution was: mesiolingual confluent (43.8%), mesiobuccal confluent (24.7%), independent (23.3%), and confluent (8.2%). MMCs were significantly more frequent in mandibular first molars (20.6%) than in second molars (6.6%) (p < 0.001). The most frequently observed MMC type was the mesiolingual confluent. In the multivariable GEE analysis, mandibular first molars had significantly higher odds of presenting an MMC than second molars (adjusted odds ratio = 3.54, 95% confidence interval: 2.16-5.80, p < 0.001), whereas age and sex were not significantly associated with MMC presence. Conclusions Within the examined single-center Turkish subpopulation and under the specific CBCT acquisition protocol used, MMCs were detected more frequently in mandibular first molars than in second molars. The mesiolingual confluent configuration was the most frequently observed morphological type. These findings highlight the anatomical variability of MMCs and support careful assessment of the mesial root canal system during endodontic treatment.

title: Prediction of PD-L1 expression in NSCLC patients based on 18F-FDG PET/CT heterogeneity scores.
abstract: Background This study aims to explore the role of radiomic features and PET image heterogeneity in predicting PD-L1 expression in NSCLC. Methods This retrospective single-center study included pathologically confirmed NSCLC patients who underwent pre-treatment 18 F-FDG PET/CT and PD-L1 immunohistochemical assessment, PD-L1 positivity was defined as a tumor proportion score (TPS) ≥1%. Metabolic heterogeneity was assessed using the coefficient of variation (COV, SUVsd / SUVmean × 100%), the distance from the hottest voxel to the tumor centroid (NHOC), and the distance from the hottest voxel to the nearest tumor boundary (NHOP). Tumors were semi-automatically segmented using a 40% SUVmax threshold. To capture the most comprehensive peritumoral information, the ROI is expanded by 15 mm. Radiomic features were extracted from intratumoral and 15-mm peritumoral regions on PET and CT images and a model is built with tumor and surrounding features using Gradient Boosting Decision Tree. The model effectiveness is assessed using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1 score. Results The study included 96 patients (median age: 64 [59, 70] years), of whom 58 were male. 63 patients were PD-L1 expression positive, while 33 were negative. COV and NHOP was significantly higher in the PD-L1 positive group (Z=-2.688, P=0.007; Z=-3.704, P<0.001), while no significant differences noted in other parameters between the groups (P>0.05 for all). Both COV and NHOP are independent predictors of PD-L1 positivity(P<0.05). The combined radiomics model outperforms the individual radiomics models, with the integrated intratumoral CT, PET, and peritumoral CT radiomics model achieving the highest predictive performance (AUC=0.816). The addition of metabolic heterogeneity parameters (COV and NHOP) further improved discrimination, resulting in all evaluation metrics exceeding 0.8. Conclusions 18 F-FDG PET/CT metabolic parameters, especially COV and NHOP, predict PD-L1 expression and improve targeted treatment decision-making.

title: Personalized dosimetry for targeted radionuclide therapy: initial clinical experience from a case series at a tertiary cancer center (King Hussein Cancer Center).
abstract: Background Targeted radionuclide therapy (TRT) plays a pivotal role in managing differentiated thyroid cancer, neuroendocrine tumors, and metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Personalized dosimetry quantifies absorbed radiation doses to tumors and organs at risk (OARs), enabling treatment individualization, improved therapeutic outcomes, and reduced toxicity. Methods This retrospective case series evaluated four patients treated at King Hussein Cancer Center (KHCC) between February 2024 and July 2025 with [ 131 I]iodine, [ 177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE, or [ 177 Lu] Lu-prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA). Patients were selected based on oligometastatic disease, adequate radiotracer uptake on baseline imaging, eligibility for radionuclide therapy, and absence of treatment contraindications. Dosimetry followed the medical internal radiation dose (MIRD) methodology with multi-timepoint imaging. Volumes of interest were segmented manually on post-therapy single photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT), time-activity curves were generated, and residence times were computed to estimate absorbed doses for tumor lesions and OARs. Treatment response was assessed using serial imaging and biochemical markers. Results The cohort included two females (aged 9 and 45 years) and two males (aged 65 and 81 years). Substantial inter- and intra-patient variability in absorbed dose and response patterns was observed. The 45-year-old female received 180 mCi (6660 MBq) of [ 131 I]iodine; skeletal metastases showed a broad dose range (~63-115 Gy), and the patient achieved a complete biochemical response. In the pediatric [ 177 Lu]Lu-DOTATATE case, the patient received 75 mCi (2775 MBq) during the third treatment cycle; lesion dose (~8.8 Gy) and renal exposure remained within safe limits, despite asymmetric renal involvement. The 81-year-old male received 100 mCi (3700 MBq) of [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA; a low lesion dose (~0.5 Gy) was observed, correlating with limited clinical benefit. The 65-year-old male received five cycles of 200 mCi (7400 MBq) [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA each; marked lesion-specific heterogeneity was observed, with high-dose lesions regressing, whereas persistent PSMA-avid lesions suggested resistance. Across all patients, OAR doses remained below safety thresholds. Conclusions Personalized dosimetry is feasible in routine clinical practice and provides critical insights into dose-response relationships. It guides treatment optimization, identifies undertreated lesions, and helps maintain OAR safety, supporting its integration into TRT workflows to enhance therapeutic precision and outcomes.

title: AIMS65, Rockall, and Glasgow-Blatchford scores for in-hospital mortality, three-month mortality, and rebleeding in patients with upper gastrointestinal bleeding. A retrospective study.
abstract: Background Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) is a potentially fatal condition. Risk stratification is a fundamental part of patient care, allowing the detection of the correct timing of treatment, correct patient allocation, and prognosis. The aim of the present study is to compare the prognostic accuracy of AIMS65, pre-endoscopy Rockall score, full Rockall score, and Glasgow-Blatchford bleeding score (GBS) in the prediction of in-hospital mortality (IHM), 3-month rebleeding, and 3-month mortality in adult patients admitted to the emergency department (ED) with a diagnosis of UGIB. Methods This is a retrospective, monocentric study. Data on IHM, recurrence of UGIB within 3 months, and 3-month mortality were collected blindly from the clinical data. Results In predicting IHM, the AIMS65 showed moderate accuracy (AUROC [area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve]=0.765 [P=0.005]), while none of the other scores had significant overall accuracy. None of the scores proved to be significantly accurate in predicting 3-month rebleeding. Only AIMS65, pre-endoscopy Rockall score, and full Rockall score showed moderate accuracy in predicting 3-month mortality (AUROC=0.77 [P=0.003], 0.75 [P=0.007], and 0.746 [P=0.008], respectively), with no differences among them. Conclusions Only AIMS65 has significant accuracy in predicting IHM. None of the included scores showed global accuracy in predicting re-bleeding within 3 months. AIMS65, pre-endoscopy Rockall, and full Rockall scores were all good at predicting death at 3 months, with no significant differences.

title: Artificial intelligence-based dental screening using a cellular phone in dogs: a practical tool for detecting visible calculus and gingivitis.
abstract: Objective To train, validate, and evaluate a cellular phone-based AI system for image-level classification of visible dental calculus and gingivitis in conscious dogs. Methods This multicenter retrospective study used dental photographs collected from 12 veterinary hospitals (2022 through 2024). Dental photographs were obtained from conscious dogs using cellular phone cameras. A single veterinarian assigned reference labels using standardized criteria. Separate binary datasets for dental calculus and gingivitis were split by dog into training, validation, and independent test datasets. A convolutional neural network was trained using transfer learning, and final models were selected by validation loss. Results A total of 3,170 dogs were included in this study. For dental calculus, 2,771 images were analyzed: 2,451 for training and validation and 320 in the independent test dataset. For gingivitis, 1,684 images were analyzed: 1,434 for training and validation and 250 in the independent test dataset. On the independent test datasets, the dental calculus model achieved precision of 0.977 (95% CI, 0.941 to 0.991), sensitivity of 0.965 (95% CI, 0.926 to 0.984), specificity of 0.973 (95% CI, 0.932 to 0.989), accuracy of 0.969 (95% CI, 0.943 to 0.983), and F1 score of 0.971. The gingivitis model achieved precision of 0.912 (95% CI, 0.855 to 0.948), sensitivity of 0.950 (95% CI, 0.901 to 0.976), specificity of 0.881 (95% CI, 0.807 to 0.929), accuracy of 0.920 (95% CI, 0.880 to 0.948), and F1 score of 0.931. Conclusions The AI system demonstrated high classification performance for visible dental calculus and gingivitis in conscious dogs. Clinical relevance This system may serve as an adjunctive screening and triage tool but is not intended to replace comprehensive oral examination or dental radiography.

title: Fluorescein sodium-guided resection of cervical peripheral nerve sheath tumors in 3 dogs.
abstract: Objective To describe the intraoperative findings and outcomes of fluorescein sodium-guided resection of cervical peripheral nerve sheath tumors (PNSTs) in dogs, including in the re-operative setting. Animals 3 client-owned dogs with cervical PNST. Two dogs underwent a second resection of progressive malignant PNST (MPNST) after subtotal resection and stereotactic radiation therapy performed elsewhere. One dog underwent primary resection of a previously untreated PNST identified as a schwannoma. Clinical presentation Affected dogs were between 10 and 11 years of age (weighing between 4.2 and 5.4 kg) and presented with cervical pain, hyperesthesia, or tetraparesis. Preoperative MRI revealed contrast-enhancing intradural extramedullary masses with extraforaminal extensions. Results Fluorescein sodium (20 mg/kg) was administered IV after surgical exposure. Tumor tissue exhibited yellow discoloration under standard illumination in all dogs and bright fluorescence under 395-nm UV illumination in 2 dogs and, in the 2 re-operative cases, was visually distinct from the surrounding postoperative and radiation-induced fibrosis, which was grossly assessed as nondiseased and did not take up fluorescein. This contrast assisted dissection, and gross total resection was achieved in all dogs; nonfluorescent tissue was not biopsied. Histopathology confirmed MPNST in 2 dogs and schwannoma in 1 dog. Fluorescein-related adverse events were not observed. Both MPNST cases developed remote or metastatic disease within 4 months (1 euthanized); the schwannoma case was recurrence-free at 3 months. Clinical relevance Fluorescein sodium-guided resection of canine cervical PNSTs is feasible with widely available equipment and may aid intraoperative identification of tumor tissue in both primary and re-operative settings, suggesting a lower equipment barrier than commonly assumed. Because nonfluorescent tissue was not sampled, fluorescein should be an adjunct to, not a substitute for, surgical judgment.

title: Exploring Factors Associated with Delayed Postoperative Skeletal Muscle Index Recovery in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Objectives Skeletal muscle index (SMI) is considered an important prognostic factor in colorectal cancer (CRC); however, the factors associated with postoperative SMI changes in patients with CRC are not clear. This study aimed to explore the factors associated with delayed postoperative SMI recovery in patients with CRC. Methods : This retrospective, observational, single-center study included 120 consecutive patients diagnosed with primary CRC and scheduled for surgery between October 2016 and September 2021. SMI was measured using computed tomography images at four perioperative time points (preoperatively, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year postoperatively). To identify factors associated with delayed postoperative SMI recovery at 1 year, logistic regression analysis was performed with delayed postoperative SMI recovery at 1 year as the dependent variable. Results Sixty-four patients with a median age of 69 years were included. Multiple logistic regression analysis revealed rectal cancer [odds ratio (OR) 3.70] and sedentary time (OR 1.27) as preoperative factors associated with delayed SMI recovery at 1 year. In an exploratory postoperative course model, the percent SMI decline from preoperative to 3 months (OR 1.20) and the delayed recovery percentage from 3 to 6 months (OR 1.19) were also significantly associated with delayed SMI recovery at 1 year. Conclusions Delayed postoperative SMI recovery at 1 year may be associated with preoperative factors including rectal cancer and sedentary time. Exploratory analysis suggested that early postoperative SMI decline and incomplete recovery between 3 and 6 months may also be related to delayed recovery at 1 year.

title: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
abstract: Background Athletic hamstring injuries (AHSI) remain a persistent challenge because recurrence is common and clinical decisions often depend on incomplete evidence. This consensus statement is intended to give clinicians a practical, unified framework for classification, rehabilitation, and return to sport after athletic hamstring injury. The purpose of this study was to achieve expert consensus on the management of athletic hamstring injuries through a structured, scientific survey approach. Study design Delphi Survey. Methods A modified Delphi process, aligned with CREDES guidelines, was conducted with an expert panel of sports physical therapists identified as having specific expertise in AHSI from the ICCUS Society. Consensus was defined a priori as at least 80% agreement or disagreement on a 5-point Likert scale. Statements addressed three areas: AHSI examination and classification, rehabilitation and management, and return to sport (RTS) testing. Results Sixty statements were developed across three domains. Seventeen experienced clinicians completed the final round. Overall, 54 statements reached consensus, with a mean Likert score of 4.56 ± 0.37 out of 5 (strongly agree), and mean agreement of 89.88% ± 12.1%. Experts supported standardized terminology, MRI and the use of diagnostic ultrasound for diagnosis when appropriate, individualized and criterion-based rehabilitation, progressive tissue loading and length restoration, early neuromuscular control, gradual running and agility progression, progression to pain-free sprinting, objective strength assessment, sport-specific workloads, and athlete readiness as key RTS criteria. Discussion The findings emphasize active rehabilitation guided by measurable progress rather than reliance on fixed thresholds. Clinicians should combine injury classification, functional presentation, symptom response, objective testing, sport demands, and athlete confidence when advancing rehabilitation and making RTS decisions. Conclusion This ICCUS Society consensus statement offers a practical roadmap for managing AHSI: classify clearly, load progressively, monitor symptoms, test objectively, and return athletes only when sport-specific running, sprinting, strength, training tolerance, and readiness align. title: Diagnostic Musculoskeletal Ultrasound in the Evaluation of the Extensor Digitorum Longus.
abstract: The extensor digitorum longus muscle and tendons are among the longer muscle-tendon units in the lower leg and foot. This feather-like, unipennate muscle is part of the anterior ankle group, attaching proximally along the lateral side of the lateral condyle of the tibia and the upper three-quarters of the fibula's inner surface. Near the ankle, the tendon narrows as it passes beneath the extensor retinacula and divides into four smaller tendons that connect to the toes. Since it crosses the ankle joint and attaches to the second through fifth toes, it facilitates dorsiflexion of the foot and extension of the toe joints. An accurate diagnosis of extensor digitorum longus tendonitis or rupture is crucial for appropriate treatment planning and optimal patient outcomes. Diagnostic musculoskeletal ultrasound (MSKUS) has become a widely used imaging modality for assessing many ankle and foot pathologies. It offers a portable, real-time, and cost-effective alternative that is gaining traction in rehabilitation and sports medicine settings. MSKUS has emerged as a valuable, non-invasive imaging modality for evaluating ankle and foot injuries. This manuscript reviews the utility of MSKUS in evaluating the quality, size, sonographic techniques, and clinical implications for rehabilitation professionals who need to visualize the extensor digitorum longus. By integrating MSKUS into clinical practice, providers can improve diagnostic accuracy, increase diagnostic confidence, monitor healing progression, and guide rehabilitation strategies to optimize outcomes for patients with ankle and foot injuries.

title: Estimating selected screening-related parameters using New Zealand-specific glaucoma prevalence data: optometry visits for glaucoma screening at age 45 years.
abstract: Background Regular eye examinations for glaucoma at age 45 years and every 5 years after have been promoted in the New Zealand setting. We aimed to estimate selected screening-related parameters for optometry visits for glaucoma screening at age 45 years. Methods Selected glaucoma screening parameters were identified from the literature, and data were extracted from a New Zealand longitudinal study (Dunedin Study) on the prevalence of glaucoma in 45-year-olds. Out-of-pocket costs were estimated from New Zealand optometry assessment fees. Results We estimate that routine screening for glaucoma within a New Zealand cohort of 45-year-olds has a low positive predictive value of 5.4%. That is, for every 100 people who get a positive screening result for glaucoma, around 95 of these diagnoses would be expected to be false positives and only five would truly have glaucoma. The number needed to screen to detect one case of glaucoma was estimated at 177. The out-of-pocket cost per true case of glaucoma detected was around NZ$24,300, equivalent to NZ$5.8 million at the national level to detect 241 true cases per year (assuming 70% uptake). However, there would be many other additional costs likely with any formal screening programme encompassing the full clinical pathway. Conclusion These New Zealand-specific findings for selected screening parameters align with recommendations from international agencies showing that there is a lack of evidence in favour of population screening for glaucoma. Future research could focus on evaluating more targeted screening or risk-based screening, e.g., using artificial intelligence-assisted fundus imaging.

title: Development of machine learning models for fetal birth weight prediction: A single-center study in a Turkish population.
abstract: Fetal birth weight (BW) is a critical indicator of the prognosis of perinatal health. Accurate estimation of BW is essential in determining the appropriate delivery method. This single-center study aims to evaluate the performance of various machine learning (ML) algorithms in estimating BW. The study population consisted of 456 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies evaluated at a single tertiary center in the Karaman region of Turkiye between 38 and 41 weeks based on their last menstrual period, who gave birth to a phenotypically normal live newborn within 7 days after the ultrasound examination. Seven out of the nine models developed using ML algorithms had the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) values ranging from 184.30 to 190.00 grams. The formula closest to these values was Hadlock III, with an MAE value of 223.33 grams. In our study, the model demonstrating the highest predictive accuracy was provided by Linear Regression algorithm with an MAE value of 184.30 grams. title: Suction Sheath-Assisted versus Conventional Endoscopic Treatment of Renal and Upper Ureteric Stones.
abstract: Objective To compare early complete stone clearance after negative-pressure suction sheath-assisted and conventional endoscopic treatment of renal or upper ureteric stones. Study design A non-randomised comparative study. Place and Duration of the Study: Central Hospital of Suining, Suining, China, from October 2025 to March 2026. Methodology The subjects comprised 115 consecutively enrolled adults with 5-20 mm stones; 58 underwent conventional endoscopy and 57 received suction sheath assistance. Complete clearance was defined as no residual fragment being recorded on postoperative imaging within two weeks. Clearance proportions were compared using an uncorrected Pearson's chi-square test. Unadjusted risk ratios and risk differences were calculated with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Adverse events and hospital stay were described for the whole cohort. Groups were classified by the technique received. Baseline characteristics were summarised for the cohort, and the comparative clearance estimate was not adjusted for potential confounders. Results Complete clearance occurred in 82/115 (71.3%) patients, including 46/58 (79.3%) after conventional treatment and 36/57 (63.2%) after suction-assisted treatment (χ2 = 3.666, p = 0.056). The risk ratio for suction-assisted versus conventional treatment was 0.80 (95% CI 0.63-1.01); the risk difference was -16.2 percentage points (95% CI -31.6 to 0.4). Postoperative fever occurred in 12/115 (10.4%) patients, haematuria in 29/115 (25.2%), and intraoperative complications in 18/115 (15.7%). The mean hospital stay was 2.3 ± 0.9 days. Conclusion Negative-pressure suction sheath assistance was not associated with significantly higher early complete stone clearance. The findings did not establish equivalence or comparative safety. Key words Kidney calculi, Ureteral calculi, Ureteroscopy, Suction, Lithotripsy, Laser.

title: Deep Learning-Based Segmentation of the Submandibular Salivary Gland on Ultrasonography.
abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate a deep learning model for automatic detection and segmentation of the submandibular salivary gland on ultrasonography using the YOLOv8x architecture. Study design A cross-sectional analytical study. Place and Duration of the Study: Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Radiology, Faculty of Dentistry, Marmara University, Istanbul, Turkiye, from March to September 2025. Methodology A total of 414 anonymised ultrasound images of normal submandibular glands were retrospectively analysed. Polygonal annotations were performed and verified by expert radiologists. The dataset was divided into training (80%), validation (10%), and test (10%) sets. A YOLOv8x-seg model was trained for 800 epochs using augmentation techniques including noise injection, contrast adjustment, and blurring. Model performance was evaluated using precision, sensitivity, F1-score, Dice coefficient, and intersection-over-union (IoU). Results The model achieved a sensitivity of 93%, a precision of 90%, and an F1-score of 0.92. Segmentation performance showed a Dice coefficient of 0.87 and an IoU of 0.78, indicating high agreement with expert annotations. Conclusion Deep learning using YOLOv8x enables accurate and efficient segmentation of the submandibular gland in ultrasound images. This approach may improve diagnostic consistency and workflow efficiency. Future studies should validate these findings using larger, multi-centre datasets including pathological cases. Key words Artificial intelligence, Deep learning, YOLOv8x, Ultrasonography, Submandibular salivary gland, Automatic detection.

title: Clinical Applications of <sup>68</sup>Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT in the Evaluation and Management of Meningiomas: A Mini Review.
abstract: Meningiomas are the most common primary intracranial tumors, and accurate imaging plays a central role in their diagnosis, risk assessment, treatment planning, and follow-up. Although many meningiomas are slow-growing, their clinical behavior can vary widely, with some tumors showing aggressive growth, postoperative recurrence, or complex extension into the skull base, bone, orbit, or dural venous sinuses. MRI and CT remain the standard imaging modalities for anatomic assessment; however, both have important limitations. MRI may be unable to reliably distinguish a residual or recurrent tumor from postoperative scarring, fibrosis, or radiation-related changes, whereas CT may be limited in differentiating reactive hyperostosis from true osseous tumor infiltration. Molecular imaging with 68 Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT has emerged as a valuable complementary technique because of its high affinity for somatostatin receptor subtype 2, which is strongly expressed in most meningiomas. By providing high lesion-to-background contrast, 68 Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT may improve lesion conspicuity and provide complementary information about disease extent in selected cases. Available evidence is strongest for problem-solving applications involving equivocal lesions and delineation of skull base, osseous, or optic nerve sheath disease, as well as confirmation of somatostatin receptor expression when receptor-targeted therapy is being considered. Other proposed applications, including tumor grading, prognostication, surgical planning, radiotherapy target refinement, quantitative response assessment, and routine surveillance, remain emerging and require prospective validation. This mini review summarizes the current applications, technical considerations, and limitations of 68 Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT in meningioma management.

title: Data-Driven Respiratory Motion Correction in <sup>18</sup>F-FDG PET for Cardiac Sarcoidosis: A Location-Dependent Phantom Study.
abstract: Respiratory motion (RM) may affect quantitative accuracy in 18 F-FDG PET for cardiac sarcoidosis (CS). Here, we evaluated the location-dependent effects of RM and RM correction (RMC) using a CS phantom with focal myocardial lesions. Methods: CS lesions were simulated by coin-shaped inserts attached to the anterior, septal, and inferior walls of a cardiac phantom. PET data were acquired under static conditions and simulated RM conditions with motion amplitudes of 10, 20, and 30 mm. RMC images were generated using data-driven respiratory gating. Both SUV max and SUV mean were measured, and percentage changes relative to static images were calculated. Results: RM caused progressive underestimation of SUV with increasing motion amplitude. The degree of SUV reduction differed with lesion location. With motion of ±15 mm, SUV max decreased by 44% in anterior, 39% in inferior, and 27% in septal walls. With motion correction of ±15 mm, SUV max reductions improved to 39% in anterior, 23% in inferior, and 6% in septal walls, with the greatest improvement observed in the latter. SUV mean showed trends similar to those of SUV max Conclusion: RM causes a region-dependent decrease in the quantitative accuracy of 18 F-FDG PET for CS lesions. Although RMC decreased SUV underestimation, a substantial underestimation remained at larger motion amplitudes. Therefore, both RM and lesion location are relevant factors to consider in quantitative PET evaluations for CS.

title: Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen PET/CT Segmentation Guided by Vision Language Models Embedding Clinical Report Semantics.
abstract: Whole-body prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT segmentation remains challenging: manual contouring is unsustainable, and image-only artificial intelligence models often misclassify physiologic uptake as malignant, causing high false-positive rates. These limitations underscore the need for segmentation strategies that incorporate the nuclear medicine expertise encoded in PET/CT reports but not used by current models. We investigated whether routine PET/CT reports improve automated lesion segmentation for prostate cancer. Methods: We developed a language-guided 3-dimensional SegResNet fusing report text with 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT image features, encoding report semantics via 4 strategies (BiomedVLP, RadGraph, GPT-raw, GPT-engineered) compared with an image-only model (baseline). Of 320 patients who underwent 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT, 297 studies were available; 13 were excluded for missing reports or incomplete image-mask pairs, leaving 284 for analysis, split at the patient level into 243 development cases and a fixed 41-case held-out test set. Metrics included Dice, intersection over union (IoU), precision, recall, average symmetric surface distance, 95th percentile Hausdorff distance, surface Dice similarity at 5 mm, and lesion-level false positives, using 3 matching criteria (any overlap; 1-to-1 maximum IoU matching, IoU ≥ 0.5; and correct localization of the SUV max voxel). Significance was assessed using paired 1-sided Wilcoxon tests with Holm adjustment. Results: Report guidance consistently reduced false positives and improved whole-mask boundary agreement. False-positive lesions were reduced by nearly 4 per patient with BiomedVLP and by approximately 3 per patient with RadGraph and GPT-raw. Average symmetric surface distance decreased from 105.4 ± 62.5 mm (image only) to 23.4 ± 18.2 mm with BiomedVLP, 36.9 ± 22.4 mm with RadGraph, and 36.3 ± 26.4 mm with GPT-raw; 95th percentile Hausdorff distance improved from 455.0 ± 169.3 mm to 123.8 ± 80.3 mm with BiomedVLP, and surface Dice similarity at 5 mm increased from 0.638 ± 0.172 to 0.705 ± 0.181. However, when these surface metrics were recomputed on matched true-positive lesions only using the same 3 criteria, no language-guided model differed significantly from the image-only model for any surface metric (all Holm-adjusted P = 1.0), indicating that the whole-mask improvements were attributable to false-positive suppression rather than genuine gains in contour accuracy on correctly detected lesions. Precision increased for BiomedVLP (0.099) and RadGraph (0.060), with a modest decrease in voxel-level recall (-0.051, BiomedVLP), reflecting a precision-recall trade-off from suppression of spurious uptake. Dice improved by 0.032 but was borderline significant; IoU increased for BiomedVLP (0.036). Lesion-level sensitivity changed by no more than 0.04 for all models and did not reach significance. Total lesion PSMA remained highly correlated with manual measurements ( r ≥ 0.85), whereas PSMA tumor volume correlations were more variable across models ( r = 0.37-0.70). Conclusion: The integration of PET/CT report semantics into automated PSMA PET/CT segmentation substantially reduced false-positive lesions and preserved total lesion PSMA agreement with manual measurements; a matched true-positive-only reanalysis indicated that the accompanying whole-mask boundary-agreement gains reflected false-positive suppression rather than improved contour accuracy on correctly detected lesions. This approach may reduce manual cleanup and support more reliable quantitative workflows, although precision gains should be weighed against a modest recall reduction. External validation, extension of the true-positive-only analysis to independent cohorts, and PSMA-specific language pretraining are warranted.

We investigated whether routine PET/CT reports improve automated lesion segmentation for prostate cancer. Methods: We developed a language-guided 3-dimensional SegResNet fusing report text with 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT image features, encoding report semantics via 4 strategies (BiomedVLP, RadGraph, GPT-raw, GPT-engineered) compared with an image-only model (baseline). Of 320 patients who underwent 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT, 297 studies were available; 13 were excluded for missing reports or incomplete image-mask pairs, leaving 284 for analysis, split at the patient level into 243 development cases and a fixed 41-case held-out test set. Metrics included Dice, intersection over union (IoU), precision, recall, average symmetric surface distance, 95th percentile Hausdorff distance, surface Dice similarity at 5 mm, and lesion-level false positives, using 3 matching criteria (any overlap; 1-to-1 maximum IoU matching, IoU ≥ 0.5; and correct localization of the SUVmax voxel). Significance was assessed using paired 1-sided Wilcoxon tests with Holm adjustment. Results: Report guidance consistently reduced false positives and improved whole-mask boundary agreement. False-positive lesions were reduced by nearly 4 per patient with BiomedVLP and by approximately 3 per patient with RadGraph and GPT-raw. Average symmetric surface distance decreased from 105.4 ± 62.5 mm (image only) to 23.4 ± 18.2 mm with BiomedVLP, 36.9 ± 22.4 mm with RadGraph, and 36.3 ± 26.4 mm with GPT-raw; 95th percentile Hausdorff distance improved from 455.0 ± 169.3 mm to 123.8 ± 80.3 mm with BiomedVLP, and surface Dice similarity at 5 mm increased from 0.638 ± 0.172 to 0.705 ± 0.181. However, when these surface metrics were recomputed on matched true-positive lesions only using the same 3 criteria, no language-guided model differed significantly from the image-only model for any surface metric (all Holm-adjusted P = 1.0), indicating that the whole-mask improvements were attributable to false-positive suppression rather than genuine gains in contour accuracy on correctly detected lesions. Precision increased for BiomedVLP (0.099) and RadGraph (0.060), with a modest decrease in voxel-level recall (-0.051, BiomedVLP), reflecting a precision-recall trade-off from suppression of spurious uptake. Dice improved by 0.032 but was borderline significant; IoU increased for BiomedVLP (0.036). Lesion-level sensitivity changed by no more than 0.04 for all models and did not reach significance. Total lesion PSMA remained highly correlated with manual measurements (r ≥ 0.85), whereas PSMA tumor volume correlations were more variable across models (r = 0.37-0.70). This approach may reduce manual cleanup and support more reliable quantitative workflows, although precision gains should be weighed against a modest recall reduction. External validation, extension of the true-positive-only analysis to independent cohorts, and PSMA-specific language pretraining are warranted.

title: An International Study of Factors Affecting Variability of Dosimetry Calculations, Part 6: Lessons Learned, Achievable Variability, and the Road Ahead.
abstract: Personalized radiopharmaceutical therapies rely on accurate and reproducible absorbed dose estimates. However, substantial variability persists because of differences in imaging protocols, segmentation, time-activity curve fitting and integration, and dose calculation implementation. The Society of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging 177 Lu Dosimetry Challenge was a 5-task international study designed to isolate sources of variability in image-based dosimetry workflows. In this final publication, we integrate findings across the series and perform a retrospective analysis of the original full-workflow submissions to estimate the reduction in variability achievable through methodologic consistency and quality assurance. Methods: In this final analysis, the original task 1 end-to-end SPECT/CT workflow submissions were reevaluated to generate a refined task 1 dataset by excluding previously identified processing or reporting mistakes, as well as submissions with methodologic choices inconsistent with the recommendations derived from the challenge. Exclusion criteria included nonstandard volume-of-interest (VOI) definitions, inconsistent VOI handling, inappropriate time-activity curve fitting and integration, and omission of required mass scaling. Variability was quantified using the interquartile range and quartile coefficient of dispersion (QCD). Results: The refined task 1 analysis showed that a substantial fraction of the observed variability is potentially avoidable. Exclusions reduced the analyzed dataset by approximately 50% and narrowed absorbed dose distributions for most organs and lesions. For patient A, QCD decreased for total kidney (23.1% to 3.0%), spleen (24.2% to 7.8%), and lesion 1 (22.8% to 13.3%). For patient B, organ variability also decreased (12.6% to 8.2% in the liver and 15.3% to 10.9% in the left kidney), although variability for some lesions decreased less substantially. Findings across the challenge indicated that, among the workflow steps evaluated, segmentation and time-activity curve fitting/integration were the dominant contributors to variability, whereas variability from the absorbed dose calculation step alone was generally small once upstream inputs were standardized. Conclusion: A substantial portion of variability in radiopharmaceutical therapy dosimetry is potentially avoidable through standardization and quality assurance. Under more standardized conditions, organ absorbed dose estimates showed markedly lower variability, with QCD values as low as 3%. These results support implementation of standardized VOI segmentation rules, time-activity curve modeling conventions, and auditable quality control and reporting procedures to improve reproducibility in both clinical trials and routine practice.

title: PDGFRβ-Targeting VHH Tracer Enables Noninvasive PET Imaging of Kidney Fibrosis.
abstract: With a prevalence above 10% worldwide, chronic kidney disease is one of the leading medical burdens. Independent of the underlying cause, kidney fibrosis emerges as the common final endpoint and serves as the most robust predictor of disease progression and long-term prognosis. Fibrosis is driven by extracellular matrix-producing mesenchymal cells, which are characterized by platelet-derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ) expression. PDGFRβ also mediates fibrogenesis in these cells and represents a potential therapeutic target for direct intervention or a potential anchor for selective delivery of antifibrotic drugs. Diagnostic approaches assessing PDGFRβ expression in kidneys are missing. Here, we developed and evaluated a novel tracer using a PDGFRβ-targeting biparatopic variable domain of a heavy-chain-only antibody construct, designated SP02SP26-ABD, for in vivo, noninvasive, molecular imaging of kidney fibrosis. Methods: PDGFRβ expression was assessed in human kidney biopsies and publicly available transcriptomic datasets. In vivo imaging studies were performed in 2 distinct murine models of kidney fibrosis using fluorescence imaging and 89 Zr-labeled PET. Specificity and dose dependency were evaluated using a nonspecific control variable domain of a heavy-chain-only antibody construct, R2R2-ABD, and coinjection of increasing amounts of unlabeled SP02SP26-ABD. Ex vivo biodistribution and correlation with histologic and molecular markers of fibrosis were performed. Results: PDGFRβ was increased in fibrotic human kidneys across multiple disease entities, predominantly localized to pericytes and fibroblasts, supporting its relevance as a translational imaging target. In vivo imaging demonstrated significantly higher tracer accumulation in fibrotic compared with nonfibrotic kidneys across both models, whereas tracer accumulation in nonrenal organs was low, with minimal uptake in the spleen. We found no difference between fibrotic and nonfibrotic kidneys when using a nonspecific R2R2-ABD control construct, whereas increasing amounts of unlabeled SP02SP26-ABD led to a dose-dependent decrease in tracer accumulation, consistent with a saturation effect. Tracer signal correlated with PDGFRβ expression, confirming the specificity of the approach. Conclusion: We provide the first proof of concept for noninvasive PET imaging of PDGFRβ-expressing fibrogenic cells in kidney disease, supporting further development of this approach for specific, noninvasive assessment of kidney fibrosis.

title: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor as a Radiotheranostic Target in Orthotopic Models of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with a 5-y survival rate of approximately 20%. Although glypican-3-targeted radiotheranostics are under development, a plurality of patients with HCC lack glypican-3 expression, underscoring the need for alternative targetable antigens. Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is overexpressed in 50%-70% of HCC tumors and represents a clinically validated therapeutic target. Here, we developed and evaluated a panitumumab-based EGFR-targeted radiotheranostic pair, [ 89 Zr]Zr-desferrioxamine-panitumumab ([ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani) for immuno-PET and [ 225 Ac]Ac-Macropa-panitumumab ([ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani) for targeted α-particle therapy, in clinically relevant orthotopic HCC models. Methods: Panitumumab was conjugated with desferrioxamine or Macropa chelators and radiolabeled with 89 Zr or 225 Ac, respectively. EGFR expression was characterized across a panel of HCC cell lines. Binding affinity, biodistribution, and tumor specificity were assessed in subcutaneous and orthotopic Huh-7 models, with EGFR-mediated targeting confirmed by blocking (200-fold molar excess of unlabeled panitumumab). Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in mice bearing orthotopic Huh-7-Luc + tumors ( n = 6 per group) after a single 9.3 kBq dose of [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani, with longitudinal monitoring by bioluminescence imaging, [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani immuno-PET, and blood chemistry. Results: [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani exhibited high-affinity binding to EGFR (dissociation constant, 0.35 nM) and demonstrated robust tumor accumulation in both subcutaneous Huh-7 (20.6 ± 2.6 %IA/g) and orthotopic Huh-7-Luc + tumors (19.3 ± 2.0 %IA/g) at 120-192 h postinjection. Biodistribution of [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani closely mirrored that of [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani across organs and tumors, with tumor uptake reduced approximately 5-fold by blocking (21.7 ± 1.1 vs. 4.5 ± 0.6 %IA/g; P < 0.0001), confirming EGFR-specific targeting. A single 9.3 kBq administration of [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani induced substantial early tumor regression and significantly prolonged median survival (70 d) compared with vehicle (28 d) and blocking (35 d) groups (log-rank P < 0.0001), with no clinically meaningful hepatotoxicity or renal toxicity. However, tumor regrowth eventually occurred in all treated mice. Conclusion: [ 89 Zr]Zr-Pani and [ 225 Ac]Ac-Pani represent a radiotheranostic pair that enables EGFR-specific imaging and targeted α-particle therapy in orthotopic HCC models. These findings establish EGFR as a promising radiotheranostic target in HCC, broadening the patient population eligible for image-guided radiopharmaceutical interventions for liver cancer.

title: PSMA Total Tumor Volume: A Simple Quantifiable Biomarker for Overall Survival Prediction-Results from the International PROMISE PET Registry.
abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET is an accurate prognostic imaging biomarker of survival in patients with prostate cancer when assessed using Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardized Evaluation (PROMISE) criteria. Previously, PSMA PET PROMISE risk nomograms were created that surpassed clinical prediction tools. In this study, we focused on the evaluation of quantifiable biomarkers to simplify and facilitate overall survival (OS) prediction. Methods: Data from patients with histologically proven prostate cancer who underwent PSMA PET between December 2012 and April 2024 at participating imaging centers worldwide and who were included in the PROMISE PET Registry by January 31, 2026, were analyzed. Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels at PSMA PET, disease stage, and OS follow-up data were collected. PSMA total tumor volume (PSMA TTV) and whole-body SUV mean were assessed using predefined SUV thresholds. PSMA total lesion uptake (PSMA TL) was calculated as PSMA TTV × SUV mean PSA level at PSMA PET adjusted for PSMA TTV was calculated as PSA × TTV. Univariate regression analysis was conducted to identify potential predictors. Prognostic accuracy of quantitative biomarkers was compared using Harrell C-indices and time-dependent concordance in the development cohort. Probabilities for 3-, 5-, and 7-y OS across PSMA TTV quartiles were derived from Kaplan-Meier curves. Subgroup analysis was conducted by cancer stage. Results: In total, 13,893 patients were included in the analysis and divided 2:1 into development ( n = 9271) and validation ( n = 4622) cohorts. The prognostic accuracy of PSMA TTV in the validation cohort (C-index, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.77-0.80) was superior to SUV mean (C-index, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.61-0.64) and PSA level at PET (C-index, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.69-0.72) and similar to PSMA TL (C-index, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.76-0.79) and PSA × TTV (C-index, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.75-0.78). In the entire cohort, the median OS for PSMA TTV quartile 1 (0 mL) and quartile 2 (>0-2.1 mL) was not reached. The median OS was 11.4 y (interquartile range, 10.1 y to not reached) for PSMA TTV quartile 3 (>2.1-16.2 mL) and 4.4 y (interquartile range, 4.2-4.6 y) for quartile 4 (>16.17 mL). Conclusion: Among quantifiable PET metrics, PSMA TTV had the highest prognostic accuracy for OS in patients with prostate cancer. Automated PSMA TTV assessment may facilitate fast and reproducible outcome prediction in the future.

title: Advances in Neuroscience in an Age of Rapid Technological and AI Innovation – Towards Integration Across Scales
abstract: Rapid technological innovation and artificial intelligence (AI) have transformed not only the resolution at which the brain can be observed, but also the questions that can be asked, shifting the field from description toward prediction, regulation and generation. Yet progress has largely advanced along parallel trajectories, and findings at one level rarely inform or constrain the next. Here, we review recent advances in three exemplary domains and propose a future-oriented framework for their integration. First, molecular and cellular neurotechnology, including synaptic proteomics, cryo-electron tomography, super-resolution microscopy, optoacoustic and ultrasound imaging, sonogenetics and molecular MRI, resolves neural processes with unprecedented specificity. Second, AI-based decoding of human brain activity yields precise signatures of complex, subjective conscious experiences in naturalistic contexts and is beginning to inform diagnosis, drug evaluation and individualized neuromodulation in mental disorders. Third, large-scale neural recordings, mechanistic whole-brain simulations, neural foundation models and AI surrogate brains are converging toward individualized digital twin brains. We argue that the next level of progress requires integrating these domains into a closed loop of reciprocal constraints, in which molecular measurements inform model parameters, human signatures define and evaluate what models must reproduce, and model predictions prioritize perturbations that can be tested across domains.

title: Enhancing Diagnostic Accuracy in Lung Cancer: Evaluating the Performance of a Cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Pulmonary Nodule Detection in Chest Radiographs.
abstract: Background Lung cancer remains a major global health challenge, and early diagnosis critically improves outcomes. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to enhance diagnostic accuracy in medical imaging, particularly for thoracic diseases. Objective This study evaluated a cutting-edge AI algorithm for detecting pulmonary nodules in chest radiographs to improve early lung cancer diagnosis. Material and methods In this analytical and experimental investigation, two datasets were used: Group1 (112120 frontal-view chest radiographs labeled for 14 thoracic diseases, including nodules) and Group2 (800 radiographs evenly split into positive and negative cases, with expert consensus labeling). The proprietary AI algorithm is based on CheXNet, a 121-layer convolutional neural network pretrained on ImageNet to initialize weights, enabling transfer learning for superior feature extraction. This model was chosen for its validated performance in thoracic disease detection, particularly in chest X-ray analysis. The datasets were divided into Type A (combining Group1 and Group2) and Type B (using only Group2) to assess performance under different conditions. A five-fold cross-validation was employed. Results The model achieved an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.73 for Type A and 0.782 for Type B. Sensitivity and specificity metrics were 0.736 and 0.592 for Type A, and 0.716 and 0.734 for Type B, respectively. Notably, the algorithm outperformed radiologists in some cases, demonstrating its capability to detect subtle or challenging nodules. Conclusion This AI algorithm shows promise as a clinical decision support tool, especially where access to experienced radiologists is limited. Further research is needed to refine the algorithm and validate use in real-world clinical workflows.

title: Liver Segmentation using Wavelet Coefficients and Level Set Algorithm.
abstract: In Computed Tomography (CT) scan, liver segmentation is crucial for diagnosing liver diseases. However, it faces challenges, such as partial volume effects, similarities in gray levels with adjacent organs, and variability in liver shapes. This technical note introduces a method combining wavelet coefficients and level set algorithms for precise liver segmentation. The proposed method integrates wavelet-based texture features with level set evolution, reducing reliance on pre-trained models and manual parameter tuning, and also demonstrates improved accuracy compared to existing approaches.

title: Machine learning prediction of meningioma grade using preoperative MRI: a large multicenter study.
abstract: Objective Preoperative knowledge of intracranial meningioma grade could significantly enhance surgical planning, but reliable noninvasive prediction remains an unmet clinical need. The aim of this study was to develop and externally validate a machine learning (ML) model incorporating traditional radiomic features, along with novel fractal and topological features, to predict WHO meningioma grade from preoperative MRI using a large multicenter cohort. Methods This retrospective diagnostic study analyzed a cohort of patients in the BraTS Meningioma Challenge. Patient data (n = 909) from 6 academic medical centers were used for model training and internal validation (n = 699) and one-time final external validation (n = 210). Tumors were segmented into three regions and radiomic features extracted across four MRI sequences. Eight different ML algorithms (e.g., based on neural networks, decision trees, clustering, and linear relationships) were tested across a total of 2889 candidate features. The primary outcome was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) for prediction of binarized WHO grade (1 vs 2 or 3). Results The final model used a support vector machine algorithm comprising 20 features and achieved an AUROC of 0.824 (95% CI 0.755-0.883) on unseen test data, with favorable calibration. Feature importance analysis revealed that topological complexity added complementary predictive value to conventional radiomics features. The final model is publicly available for anyone to use. Conclusions This externally validated ML model accurately predicted meningioma grade using routine preoperative MRI, with the potential to guide surgical decision-making and serve as a basis for future imaging-based brain tumor classifications.

title: Radiation-induced versus sporadic cerebral cavernous malformations: comparative analysis of incidence and hemorrhage risk.
abstract: Objective Radiation exposure has emerged as a recognized risk factor for cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM). Radiation-induced CCM (XRT-CCM) may arise months to decades after treatment and may carry higher hemorrhage risk than non-XRT-CCM, though studies remain limited. This study aimed to compare clinical characteristics, hemorrhage rates, and surgical management between XRT-CCM and non-XRT-CCM. Methods A single-institution retrospective cohort study examined patients with MRI-confirmed CCM (1987-2024). All XRT-CCM and non-XRT-CCM patients, regardless of presentation type, were included. The primary outcome was symptomatic hemorrhage following diagnosis, and the secondary outcome was surgical intervention. Analysis included descriptive statistics, group comparisons, hemorrhage incidence, multivariable logistic regression for hemorrhage risk, and Cox regression for hemorrhage-free survival. Results The cohort comprised 612 patients: 16 XRT-CCM and 596 non-XRT-CCM patients. The XRT-CCM group included 11 incidental (68.8%) and 5 non-seizure-associated hemorrhage (31.3%) presenters, while the non-XRT-CCM group included 336 incidental (56.4%), 123 non-seizure-associated hemorrhage (20.6%), and 137 seizure (23.0%) presenters. Demographic characteristics were similar between groups. XRT-CCM patients received radiation at a median age of 11.9 years, with diagnosis a median of 13.5 years later. The mean ± SD radiation dosage was 47.8 ± 15.1 Gy, most commonly for arteriovenous malformations (31%). Multivariable analysis showed that radiation was significantly associated with hemorrhage (OR 5.23, 95% CI 1.35-20.36), while presentation type was not. Hemorrhage incidence was 7.77 per 100 person-years for XRT-CCM patients versus 4.36 for non-XRT-CCM patients (incidence rate ratio 1.78). Surgical intervention rates did not differ significantly between groups (25.0% vs 21.1%), nor did primary surgical indications, with hemorrhage being the most common indication in both XRT-CCM (75.0%) and non-XRT-CCM (43.7%) patients. Conclusions XRT-CCM demonstrated a higher hemorrhage incidence compared to non-XRT-CCM, with radiation exposure significantly associated with symptomatic hemorrhage. However, radiation exposure was not significantly associated with time to hemorrhage on survival analysis. The extended latency from radiation to CCM diagnosis underscores the need for long-term surveillance in patients exposed to cranial irradiation.

title: Posterior fossa decompression in pediatric Chiari malformation type I: a meta-analysis and meta-regression of outcomes with and without duraplasty.
abstract: Objective The role of duraplasty in posterior fossa decompression for pediatric Chiari malformation type I (CM-I) remains controversial. Proponents of posterior fossa decompression with duraplasty (PFDD) argue that it improves CSF flow and syrinx regression, while posterior fossa decompression only (PFDO) is thought to offer a less invasive alternative with fewer complications. The authors investigated whether adding duraplasty provides patient-relevant clinical benefit in children with CM-I. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative pediatric studies (PFDD vs PFDO) was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Primary outcomes were overall clinical improvement, syrinx regression, Chicago Chiari Outcome Scale (CCOS) score, complications, and reoperation. Random-effects models, study-level meta-regression, graft-type subgroup analyses, and prespecified sensitivity analyzes were performed, including restriction to rigorously defined congenital CM-I cohorts and studies routinely using intraoperative ultrasound. Formal assessments of risk of bias, publication bias, and certainty of evidence were also conducted. Results Twenty-six studies consisting of 5977 pediatric patients (2641 PFDO, 3336 PFDD) were included. Clinical improvement (70.8% PFDO, 80.0% PFDD; p = 0.13), syrinx improvement (55.4% PFDO, 63.5% PFDD; p = 0.11), CCOS scores (p = 0.39), and reoperation (risk ratio [RR] 1.54, 95% CI 0.93-2.54; p = 0.09) showed no significant intergroup difference. PFDD was associated with substantially higher CSF-related morbidity (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.28-0.78; p < 0.01) and longer operative time (mean difference [MD] 63.9 minutes) and hospital stay (MD 1.22 days). No consistent differences emerged by graft type. Meta-regression showed that higher cohort-level syrinx prevalence correlated with greater clinical improvement after PFDD (p < 0.05) but not PFDO. Sensitivity analyses restricted to rigorously defined congenital CM-I cohorts and studies routinely performing intraoperative ultrasound reproduced all primary findings. Most studies were retrospective with moderate to serious risk of bias and overall certainty of evidence graded as moderate. No significant publication bias was detected (p = 0.36). The role of duraplasty in posterior fossa decompression for pediatric Chiari malformation type I (CM-I) remains controversial. Proponents of posterior fossa decompression with duraplasty (PFDD) argue that it improves CSF flow and syrinx regression, while posterior fossa decompression only (PFDO) is thought to offer a less invasive alternative with fewer complications. The authors investigated whether adding duraplasty provides patient-relevant clinical benefit in children with CM-I.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative pediatric studies (PFDD vs PFDO) was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Primary outcomes were overall clinical improvement, syrinx regression, Chicago Chiari Outcome Scale (CCOS) score, complications, and reoperation. Random-effects models, study-level meta-regression, graft-type subgroup analyses, and prespecified sensitivity analyzes were performed, including restriction to rigorously defined congenital CM-I cohorts and studies routinely using intraoperative ultrasound. Formal assessments of risk of bias, publication bias, and certainty of evidence were also conducted.

Results

Twenty-six studies consisting of 5977 pediatric patients (2641 PFDO, 3336 PFDD) were included. Sensitivity analyses restricted to rigorously defined congenital CM-I cohorts and studies routinely performing intraoperative ultrasound reproduced all primary findings. Most studies were retrospective with moderate to serious risk of bias and overall certainty of evidence graded as moderate. No significant publication bias was detected (p = 0.36).

Conclusions

PFDD and PFDO yielded broadly comparable clinical and radiographic outcomes in pediatric CM-I, although PFDD was associated with higher CSF-related morbidity and greater operative burden. Current evidence does not clearly define patient subgroups that derive additional benefit from duraplasty, and observed differences are likely influenced by underlying cohort heterogeneity. title: A proposed classification system for intramedullary spinal cord arteriovenous malformations that informs surgical strategy.
abstract: Objective An anatomical classification system is proposed to characterize spinal arteriovenous malformations (SpAVMs) using preoperative digital subtraction angiography (DSA) and MRI to guide surgical strategy for each SpAVM type. Methods A consecutive, single-surgeon series of 52 intra- and perimedullary SpAVMs resected over 17 years was reviewed. DSA, MRI, intraoperative videography, and digital photography findings were analyzed to classify SpAVMs into 5 types on the basis of arterial supply (anterior spinal artery, posterior spinal artery, or both), depth within the cord parenchyma (pial or intramedullary), and anatomical location (anterior, posterior, concentric [entirely intramedullary], or eccentric [intramedullary and presenting to or through the pial surface]). Results SpAVMs were classified into 5 types as follows: type 1, posterior pial (11/52, 21%); type 2, anterior pial (11/52, 21%); type 3, anterior intramedullary (7/52, 13%); type 4, concentric intramedullary (4/52, 8%); and type 5, eccentric extra- and intramedullary (17/52, 33%). Two SpAVMs were unclassifiable. Extramedullary resection was used with types 1 and 2 pial SpAVMs (20/21, 95%) and all 17 eccentric type 5 SpAVMs. Cord rotation was applied for types 2 (8/11, 73%) and 5 (13/17, 76%). Midline myelotomy was used with all type 3 (7/7) and type 4 (4/4) SpAVMs, whereas perinidal myelotomy was used with type 5 SpAVMs (14/17, 82%). Intramedullary resection was used with all type 3 (n = 7) and type 4 (n = 4) SpAVMs and most type 5 SpAVMs (14/17, 82%). In situ occlusion was used for holomedullary SpAVMs. Algorithms recommended by the classification system were applied in 86% of cases, resulting in complete SpAVM resection or angiographic obliteration in 83% of patients (43/52). At the last follow-up, 33 (65%) surviving patients were intact or had mild motor or sensory deficits (McCormick grade 1 or 2); 18 (35%) patients had moderate or severe deficits or quadriplegia/paraplegia (McCormick grade ≥ 3). Overall, 3 of 51 (6%) patients experienced deterioration relative to preoperative baseline to dependent status (McCormick grade ≥ 3). Conclusions The proposed classification system clarifies the SpAVM pathology and guides the application of surgical techniques, thereby defining surgical strategies for each SpAVM type. This classification delineates intra- and perimedullary SpAVMs by expansion from 2 to 5 categories. The proposed classification system differentiates the spectrum of SpAVM pathoanatomy, guiding resection technique by type-specific algorithms. The classification does not predict surgical risk, patient outcome, or natural history.

title: Intraoperative artificial intelligence for brain tumor surgery: from tissue diagnosis to real-time surgical guidance.
abstract: The 2021 WHO CNS tumor classification marked a fundamental shift in neuro-oncology: molecular markers rather than histological appearance now define glioma diagnosis and guide treatment. Yet, in clinical practice the molecular information that matters most to a surgeon-IDH status, 1p/19q codeletion, and methylation class-typically arrives days to weeks after the operation it was meant to inform. Artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to close that gap. Over the past several years, a growing body of work has demonstrated that AI models can extract diagnostically relevant molecular and histological information from data sources available in the operating room, in real time, at the point of surgical decision-making. In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art intraoperative AI models available to neurosurgeons during brain tumor resections. They examine AI-augmented approaches to established intraoperative techniques, such as cryosection and fluorescence-guided surgery, before turning to novel technologies including nanopore sequencing and stimulated Raman histology (SRH). The authors conclude by discussing barriers to widespread clinical adoption and what lies ahead for this field. For cryosection, models such as LGNet and the Cryosection Histopathology Assessment and Review Machine (CHARM) have demonstrated strong performance on intraoperative discrimination of primary CNS lymphoma and molecular subtyping of glioma, respectively, with CHARM achieving areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.88-0.93 across glioma subtypes. In fluorescence-guided surgery, hyperspectral imaging combined with machine learning has enabled classification of tumor type, grade, and IDH mutation based on the 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) signal with up to 93% accuracy, extracting molecular information from a modality already present in the operating room. For nanopore-based methylation classification, ensemble models such as Rapid Nanopore Brain Intraoperative Classification (ROBIN) have achieved 90% concordance with the final diagnosis prospectively in under 2 hours. In SRH, foundation models for infiltration detection now outperform FLAIR, contrast enhancement, and 5-ALA fluorescence in identifying tumor margins, while molecular classification models have achieved over 90% glioma subtype accuracy in multi-institutional cohorts. At the single-cell level, morphometric profiling of SRH images has revealed nuclear features distinguishing IDH-mutant from IDH-wildtype tumors, opening new avenues for interpretability. Despite this progress, widespread adoption remains limited by the absence of randomized clinical trials demonstrating patient-level benefit. Addressing this gap and realizing the potential of multimodal AI systems that integrate imaging, pathology, and molecular data represent critical next steps for the field.

title: Sequential arterial feeder targeting with microscope-based augmented reality and multimodal navigation for brain arteriovenous malformation resection: an integrated operative workflow in 158 cases.
abstract: Objective Early proximal arterial control is an established principle of brain arteriovenous malformation (bAVM) microsurgery but remains difficult to execute when feeding arteries are deep, obscured, or not apparent at the cortical surface. Herein, the authors describe the longitudinal clinical implementation of a workflow using multimodal navigation and microscope-based augmented reality (AR) to identify and target arterial feeders before substantial nidal dissection in bAVM resections. Methods Case-specific multimodal datasets were assembled according to clinical relevance and availability from CTA, high-resolution structural MRI with thin-slice T2-weighted imaging, MRA, and 3D rotational DSA studies and were fused within standard clinical neuronavigation platforms. All angiographically identifiable arterial feeders were segmented along their surgically relevant courses, prioritized as operative targets, and incorporated into exposure and corridor planning. Targets were displayed intraoperatively using the available navigation configuration, including microscope-based AR as the technology evolved. Functional MRI (fMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) were coregistered selectively to provide cortical and tractographic context. Consecutive navigation-assisted bAVM resections performed by a single neurosurgeon from 2013 to 2025 were analyzed. Outcomes included angiographic obliteration, perioperative morbidity, mortality, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score change relative to baseline. Results Of 192 bAVM resections performed during the study period, 158 consecutive navigation-assisted resections comprised the analytical cohort and included Spetzler-Martin (SM) grades I-V. Complete obliteration on initial angiography after microsurgery was observed in 97.5% of cases (154/158). At a median follow-up of 15 months, 93.0% of patients were functionally independent (mRS score 0-2). An increase in the mRS score relative to baseline occurred in 18.4% of patients, most commonly reflecting minor, nondisabling deficits with preserved independence. Loss of independence attributable to surgery occurred in 3.1% of patients, and the mortality rate was 1.3%. Conclusions Multimodal navigation with microscope-based AR was implemented longitudinally to identify and target arterial feeders before substantial nidal dissection, with selective integration of fMRI and DTI providing cortical and tractographic context for lesions near eloquent anatomy. Across SM grade I-V bAVMs, the workflow was feasible and was associated with high rates of angiographic obliteration and functional independence. By translating preoperative angioarchitecture into a planned sequence of discrete intraoperative arterial targets within their structural and functional context, the featured workflow provides a structured framework for operative planning, execution, and teaching in feeder-directed bAVM microsurgery.
