originalAbstract:
Background

Intramedullary spinal cord metastasis (ISCM) from gastric adenocarcinoma is extremely rare, and treatment is not standardized.

Case presentation

A 59-year-old man with a 22-month history of gastric adenocarcinoma developed acute quadriplegia during systemic therapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI showed a C3-C4 intramedullary enhancing lesion with extensive edema, and ISCM was suspected on clinical and radiological grounds. Because of the high cervical location and surgical risk, the patient received intensity-modulated radiotherapy (40 Gy in 20 fractions) with sintilimab, nab-paclitaxel, and capecitabine; dexamethasone and mannitol were used for spinal cord edema. Grade 4 neutropenia with febrile neutropenia occurred on radiotherapy day 3, and chemotherapy was stopped. Neurological function improved by radiotherapy day 10. Follow-up cervical MRI showed complete radiographic resolution of the lesion, and limb strength recovered to grade 5. The patient died approximately 6 months after the suspected ISCM diagnosis, about 3 weeks after the last cervical MRI; death was clinically attributed to cachexia from systemic tumor progression, without autopsy.

Conclusion

This case showed temporary neurological and radiographic improvement after a multimodal non-surgical approach, but it does not establish the efficacy of an individual treatment component or an overall survival benefit.

title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging: a mini review of current applications and future directions.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new opportunities to enhance medical imaging in pediatric oncology through quantitative image analysis and clinical decision support. This mini review examines the emerging role of AI in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging, including applications in lesion detection and characterization, tumor segmentation and volumetric analysis, treatment planning, longitudinal surveillance, prognostication, and precision medicine. Particular attention is given to the challenges of translating these approaches to pediatric populations, where rare and heterogeneous tumors, limited datasets, variable imaging protocols, and insufficient multicenter validation remain important barriers. We also discuss emerging strategies that may facilitate clinical translation, including federated learning, multimodal data integration, explainable AI, and integration with existing radiology workflows. Although pediatric-specific evidence remains limited, continued multicenter collaboration and prospective validation may enable AI-based tools to provide more reproducible quantitative imaging assessment and increasingly personalized clinical decision support. Ultimately, the clinical value of these technologies will depend on their ability to augment radiologist expertise and improve patient care through responsible integration into routine practice.

title: Primary hydatid disease of the rib mimicking a chest wall tumor: a case report and structured review of the literature.
abstract: Rationale Bone hydatid disease is rare, accounting for only 0.5% to 2.5% of all hydatid localizations, and costal (rib) involvement represents only a small fraction of these bone cases. Because clinical and radiological features are nonspecific, rib echinococcosis is easily mistaken for a primary or secondary bone tumor, and the diagnosis is frequently established only after surgical exploration. Case presentation A 60-year-old woman, a farmer from a rural, endemic area of northwestern Tunisia, presented with a painless, slowly enlarging swelling over the eighth right rib of two months' duration, unaccompanied by fever, weight loss, or other systemic symptoms. Ultrasonography and computed tomography of the chest wall showed an expansile osteolytic lesion of the eighth rib with cortical rupture, heterogeneous multiloculated fluid content, and an exophytic vesicle; mild hypereosinophilia was present and hydatid serology (ELISA) was moderately positive. Plasmacytoma/myeloma and bone metastasis were excluded by protein electrophoresis, breast imaging and positron emission tomography. Intraoperative findings and parasitological examination of the cyst fluid (protoscoleces and hooklets) confirmed cystic echinococcosis. A diagnosis of primary costal cystic echinococcosis was retained. Interventions The patient underwent a right lateral thoracotomy centered on the lesion with segmental resection of the affected eighth rib, debridement of adjacent soft tissue, and 20% hypertonic saline protection and irrigation to prevent local seeding, followed by three 1-month cycles of oral albendazole (400 mg twice daily). Outcomes The postoperative course was uneventful. The patient was discharged on postoperative day three and remained symptom-free, with no clinical, imaging or serological evidence of recurrence at two years of structured follow-up (clinical examination, chest-wall ultrasonography, CT and serology, the ELISA becoming negative at 24 months). Conclusion Rib hydatidosis should be included in the differential diagnosis of an osteolytic costal lesion in patients from endemic areas, even when systemic symptoms and inflammatory markers are absent and serology is negative. In our experience, complete segmental resection respecting the principles of hydatid surgery, combined with albendazole, was associated with a favorable outcome at 2 years; longer follow-up is required because late recurrences of bone echinococcosis are well documented.

title: Association of preoperative frailty, inflammatory markers and CT radiomics with complications after esophagectomy in older adults: a five-year retrospective analysis and online dynamic nomogram development.
abstract: Objective Older adults with esophageal cancer have poor physiological tolerance and a high risk of postoperative complications. This study examined whether preoperative frailty, hematologic inflammatory indices and CT radiomic features independently predict these complications and built a validated web-based nomogram for personalized risk prediction. Methods This five-year retrospective study included 526 patients aged at least 60 years who underwent radical esophagectomy between 2019 and 2023. Frailty was assessed with the Fried phenotype, five inflammatory indices were calculated from preoperative blood counts, and CT radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced chest CT. Because the five indices share the same four cell counts, their collinearity was diagnosed and the indices were compared through sequential selection, single-index and alternative-model discrimination, reclassification metrics, and order-reversed and bootstrap validation. Independent predictors were identified by two-stage multivariable logistic regression, ranked with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and assembled into a nomogram; discrimination, calibration and net clinical benefit were evaluated in training and validation cohorts. Results Complications occurred in 187 of 526 patients (35.55%). The five inflammatory indices were strongly collinear; across all sensitivity analyses the systemic inflammation response index and systemic immune-inflammation index were retained independently of entry order, whereas the neutrophil-, platelet- and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios added no incremental information. Frailty, the two retained composite indices and three CT radiomic features (lesion texture heterogeneity, gray-level mean value and shape irregularity) were independent predictors, with frailty carrying the greatest SHAP weight. The nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.824 (95% confidence interval 0.780-0.868) and 0.807 (0.746-0.868) in the training and validation cohorts, with good calibration and net clinical benefit, and it was implemented as a web tool. Conclusion Preoperative frailty, inflammatory indices and CT radiomic features are independent predictors of postoperative complications, with distinct contributions revealed by SHAP. The validated web nomogram reliably stratifies risk and supports individualized perioperative management.

title: AV-MapNet: geodesic vessel tokenization and sequential refinement for retinal vessel segmentation and artery-vein classification.
abstract: Accurate retinal vessel segmentation and artery-vein (A/V) classification are important for quantitative analysis of retinal vascular morphology, yet remain challenging in thin vessels, bifurcations, crossings, low-contrast regions, and pathological structures. This work proposes AV-MapNet, a structure-aware deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale vessel extraction, sequential residual refinement, Geodesic Vessel Tokenization (GVT), topology-aware token reasoning, and vessel-guided A/V classification. The retinal vascular tree is first extracted using a residual encoder-decoder with multi-scale dilated context and progressively corrected through recurrent vessel refinement. GVT then organizes intermediate features into vessel-aligned tokens according to refined vessel probability, local orientation, boundary ambiguity, and junction information using differentiable geodesic propagation. The resulting tokens undergo structure-biased long-range reasoning and are reconstructed into dense contextual features for subsequent A/V classification. Independent artery and vein branches are conditioned on the refined vessel representation and undergo class-specific sequential refinement before joint normalization. AV-MapNet achieved vessel segmentation DSC values of 83.01%, 85.21%, and 87.10% on RITE, HRF, and DRIVE, respectively, with corresponding accuracies of 97.67%, 98.01%, and 98.52%. Structural evaluation on the 20-image DRIVE test set yielded a clDice of 0.8490±0.0194 , with Betti-0 and Betti-1 errors of 0.9071±0.1890 and 0.2391±0.1066 , respectively. For direct binary A/V classification on valid labelled vessel pixels, AV-MapNet achieved accuracies of 96.01%, 96.48%, and 97.20% on LES-AV, AV-DRIVE, and RITE, respectively. These results demonstrate that combining sequential refinement with vessel-conditioned geodesic representation provides an effective framework for structurally informed retinal vascular analysis.

title: Structural and functional network changes following thalamotomy for focal dystonia: a multimodal MRI study.
abstract: Converging evidence supports dystonia as a disorder of large-scale brain networks arising from dysfunction within, or impaired communication between, nodes of the cortico-basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical and cerebello-thalamo-cortical circuits. Focal hand dystonia is associated with abnormalities across cortical and subcortical networks. High intensity focused ultrasound (HiFU) offers a novel therapeutic approach that provides an opportunity to examine treatment related structural and functional network changes. Eleven individuals with focal hand dystonia, of musician's dystonia and writer's cramp subtype, underwent multimodal MRI, including structural analysis, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) at baseline, with comparison made to ten age- and sex-matched healthy control participants. These imaging metrics were repeated at 1, 3 and 12 months following HiFU ventro-oral (Vo)-complex thalamotomy. This trial was registered with the Australia New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12622000775718p). No differences in regional volumes were observed at baseline between the groups. Following thalamotomy, small uncorrected volumetric changes were noted in several regions of interest, and DTI demonstrated lower tract-wise fractional anisotropy (FA) and coefficient of linearity (CL) within the treated pallidothalamic tract, with node-wise analysis demonstrating focal microstructural alterations that were most apparent at 12 months following treatment. There were no corresponding changes in fronto-striatal or fronto-thalamic tracts. rs-fMRI revealed baseline alterations in intra- and inter-network connectivity involving sensorimotor, visual, attentional, default mode and executive networks. Following thalamotomy, changes in functional connectivity were modest and temporally variable, without evidence of large-scale network reorganisation. These findings suggest that focal hand dystonia is associated with distributed functional network dysfunction, in the context of preserved macroscopic structure. We propose that Vo-complex thalamotomy is associated with focal, localized microstructural alterations within the pallidothalamic tract, most notable at 12 months, which may contribute to modulation of pathological pallidothalamic drive rather than widespread restoration of functional network connectivity.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging-based artificial intelligence in identifying imaging phenotypes of non-secondary trigeminal neuralgia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Conventional visual magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessment of neurovascular compression may overlook subtle trigeminal nerve abnormalities. We evaluated the pooled discriminative performance of MRI-based artificial intelligence (AI) models for identifying pain-related trigeminal nerve phenotypes in non-secondary trigeminal neuralgia. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to April 2026. Eligible studies developed or validated MRI-based radiomics or AI models and provided sufficient information to construct or approximate 2 × 2 contingency tables. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. Sensitivity and specificity were jointly pooled using a bivariate random-effects model, and a summary receiver operating characteristic curve was constructed. Results Eight studies comprising 628 nerve-level observations (298 symptomatic or affected nerves and 330 comparator nerves) were included. Pooled sensitivity was 0.83 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78-0.87), pooled specificity was 0.81 (95% CI, 0.74-0.86), and the summary area under the curve was 0.86 (95% CI, 0.82-0.88). Results remained stable after leave-one-out analysis. Radiomics-only models and models combining radiomic and anatomical features showed broadly comparable performance. Conclusions Preliminary evidence suggests that MRI-based AI models provide moderate discriminative ability for identifying the affected nerve side in trigeminal neuralgia, with relatively stable sensitivity but lower specificity. Given the limited number of studies, particularly in subgroup analyses, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Such models may currently serve as adjunctive imaging tools. Larger multicenter studies with independent external validation and clinically relevant reference standards are needed.

title: LARU-net: lesion-aware residual attention U-net for binary cucumber leaf lesion segmentation and continuous severity estimation.
abstract: Plant leaf diseases threaten agricultural productivity and motivate accurate automated monitoring. This study presents LARU-Net, a unified architecture for binary cucumber lesion segmentation (lesion versus background) with an auxiliary continuous severity-regression output on a bounded 0-4 scale. The network integrates a Disease Feature Enhancement Autoencoder, Residual Multi-Scale Encoder, transformer bottleneck, Attention-Guided Decoder, and Boundary Refinement Module. On the declared held-out test partition (1,080 images), the archived full-model results were Dice 0.9230, IoU 0.8660, Boundary F1 0.9350, and precision 0.9460; the previously emphasized Dice value of 0.9456 is a validation value and is now identified as such. Severity estimates yielded an overall MAE of 0.29, RMSE of 0.37, and R 2 of 0.90. These values are single-run point estimates from one greenhouse image collection. Plant/session identifiers, complete acquisition and annotation provenance, repeated-run logs, and an external dataset were not preserved in the supplied study archive; therefore, the results support in-domain evaluation but not broad cross-greenhouse or cross-season generalization. The split was stratified at image level; independence at plant, leaf, or acquisition-session level could not be verified. Confidence intervals and significance tests were not reconstructed because per-image predictions and repeated-run logs were unavailable.

title: StoneXAI-Net: an explainable weakly supervised framework for kidney stone classification, localization, and segmentation from CT images.
abstract: Introduction Kidney stone disease (urolithiasis) is one of the most frequent urological diseases worldwide; it is highly recurrent and carries a significant clinical burden and economic cost. Non-contrast computed tomography (CT) is the primary diagnostic modality and offers the highest sensitivity and specificity. However, automated kidney stone analysis remains challenging because expert pixel-level annotations are scarce, hyperdense non-stone anatomy causes mislocalization in weakly supervised localization, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are often used circularly, both for weakly supervised localization and for its subsequent interpretation. Methods We present StoneXAI-Net, an explainable, weakly supervised framework to classify, localize, and segment kidney stones from CT images. The framework consists of three modules: (i) a CT-physics augmentation strategy that diversifies training and mitigates overfitting; (ii) consensus pseudo-labeling that combines complementary explanation maps with uncertainty maps and anatomical priors to suppress false localizations; and (iii) a faithfulness audit module with deletion, insertion, and pointing-game metrics that objectively evaluates explanation quality. The resulting consensus pseudo-labels were used to train an attention-prior-conditioned Attention U-Net for segmentation. The framework was evaluated on 3,364 axial abdominal CT images (1,577 stone and 1,787 normal) using five-fold cross-validation. Results StoneXAI-Net achieved 97.4% accuracy, 98.4% precision, 96.0% recall, a 97.1% F1-score, and a 99.5% AUC. Against consensus pseudo-masks, the full segmentation configuration achieved a proxy Dice coefficient of 0.834, an IoU of 0.777, and an HD95 of 2.94 px; anatomical post-processing reduced HD95 by 6.26 px. Discussion StoneXAI-Net is a feasible and interpretable framework for the automated analysis of kidney stones that substantially reduces the time-consuming and costly manual annotation of kidney stones by experts. Because segmentation was evaluated against pseudo-masks at the slice level, these results are proxy estimates that require confirmation with expert annotations and patient-level validation.

The framework consists of three modules: (i) a CT-physics augmentation strategy that diversifies training and mitigates overfitting; (ii) consensus pseudo-labeling that combines complementary explanation maps with uncertainty maps and anatomical priors to suppress false localizations; and (iii) a faithfulness audit module with deletion, insertion, and pointing-game metrics that objectively evaluates explanation quality. The resulting consensus pseudo-labels were used to train an attention-prior-conditioned Attention U-Net for segmentation. The framework was evaluated on 3,364 axial abdominal CT images (1,577 stone and 1,787 normal) using five-fold cross-validation.

Results

StoneXAI-Net achieved 97.4% accuracy, 98.4% precision, 96.0% recall, a 97.1% F1-score, and a 99.5% AUC. Against consensus pseudo-masks, the full segmentation configuration achieved a proxy Dice coefficient of 0.834, an IoU of 0.777, and an HD95 of 2.94 px; anatomical post-processing reduced HD95 by 6.26 px.

Discussion

StoneXAI-Net is a feasible and interpretable framework for the automated analysis of kidney stones that substantially reduces the time-consuming and costly manual annotation of kidney stones by experts. Because segmentation was evaluated against pseudo-masks at the slice level, these results are proxy estimates that require confirmation with expert annotations and patient-level validation.

title: Hybrid one-shot and vertical federated learning framework for privacy-preserving brain tumor classification and segmentation using the BRISC2025 dataset.
abstract: Introduction From MRI images, diagnosis of brain tumors may have limitations due to restriction over patient privacy and lack of annotated datasets so that models cannot be trained across multiple institutions. Methods HOS-VFL: A Hybrid One-Shot and Vertical Federated Learning framework with a two-round protocol that jointly enjoys the advantages of prototype-based one-shot aggregation and encrypted vertical feature space augmentation. Tested on BRISC2025 MRimages of glioma, meningioma, pituitary and non-tumor, with T1-weighted images, expert-annotated, at five simulated institutions, with simulated IID and Dirichlet setups. Results HOS-VFL obtained values of 98.73% on accuracy and 35-50 for conventional federated learning, with a 94.3% reduction compared to the best baseline valued. HOS-VFL performed 98.73% accuracy and 35-50 for the conventional federated learning with an improvement of 94.3% when compared with its best baseline accuracy. The mean Dice and IoU of Segmentation was 0.9147, 0.8423 respectively. Performance did not wane differently in terms of competitive levels and number of institutions, and was able to withstand gradient inference attacks. Discussion HOS-VFL philosophy is centralised performance with minimum communication with retention of raw data local. The method needs to be validated on larger real multi-center datasets before their clinical use.

title: Hemodynamic changes after artificial vessel reconstruction for common iliac artery aneurysm: a case report.
abstract: Objectives Isolated iliac artery aneurysms (IIAA) frequently coexist with abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), yet their causal association remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate hemodynamic alterations following artificial vessel reconstruction for iliac aneurysm and its impact on the abdominal aorta and iliac artery. Case presentation A 54-year-old man with a history of thyroid adenoma presented with left lower abdominal pain. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed an aneurysm involving the entire left common iliac artery (48 mm × 55 mm × 81 mm). The patient was hemodynamically stable, with unremarkable physical examination and laboratory findings. He underwent aneurysm resection and aortoiliac reconstruction with a synthetic graft. Intraoperatively, arterial tortuosity and marked dilation at the bifurcation were noted. Postoperative CTA confirmed graft patency, and the patient recovered uneventfully. Preoperative and postoperative CTA scans were used for three-dimensional vascular reconstruction, followed by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to assess hemodynamic parameters including wall shear stress (WSS), blood pressure, and flow velocity. Conclusion Prosthetic vascular reconstruction for common iliac artery aneurysm (CIAA) may produce dual hemodynamic effects on the abdominal aorta. While the causal link between CIAA and AAA is unproven, the surgery eliminates rupture risk of the target aneurysm. These exploratory results may provide hemodynamic references to optimize surgical planning for iliac artery aneurysms.

title: Endoscope-assisted vs. conventional anterior cervical discectomy and fusion for single-level degenerative cervical disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Endoscope-assisted anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (EA-ACDF) has been introduced as a modified technique for the treatment of degenerative cervical disease, but its comparative efficacy and safety relative to conventional ACDF (CA-ACDF) remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare EA-ACDF with CA-ACDF for single-level degenerative cervical disease. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, WanFang, VIP, and SinoMed were searched from inception through September 7, 2026. Comparative studies of EA-ACDF vs. CA-ACDF were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Results Eleven retrospective comparative studies involving 755 patients were included. Compared with CA-ACDF, EA-ACDF was associated with longer operative time (MD = 17.31 min, 95% CI 11.38-23.23), but lower intraoperative blood loss (MD = -17.31 mL, 95% CI -24.38 to -10.25), postoperative drainage volume (MD = -10.97 mL, 95% CI -16.98 to -4.96), length of hospital stay (MD = -0.67 days, 95% CI -1.16 to -0.17), and overall complication rate (RR = 0.44, 95% CI 0.25-0.78). No significant between-group differences were observed in final Japanese Orthopaedic Association score, Neck Disability Index, visual analogue scale score, cervical lordosis, or fusion rate. The certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low. Conclusion EA-ACDF may offer modest perioperative advantages at the cost of longer operative time, while short- to mid-term clinical, radiographic, and fusion outcomes appear broadly similar. Current evidence does not establish clinical superiority. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251123475, identifier CRD420251123475.

title: Computer-Aided Diagnosis System for Sow Pregnancy Using Low-Frequency Portable Ultrasound Videos with Preprocessing and Augmentation Techniques.
abstract: Accurate pregnancy diagnosis is important for reproductive management in pig farming. This study evaluated a computer-aided diagnosis workflow using portable low-frequency ultrasound videos from 1895 sows at two sites. Xception frame predictions were aggregated into video-level decisions. Original, Preprocessing (wavelet denoising and contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization), Mixup, and their combination (Combined) were compared across ten repeated sow-level splits. Combined achieved mean accuracies of 84.5% and 85.3% in Datasets A and B, respectively, with pregnant-sow videos restricted to days 18-25 post-insemination. Compared with Original, mean specificity increased by 1.3 and 2.4 percentage points and Youden's index by 1.7 and 2.3 points, while mean sensitivity was numerically similar. Paired 95% confidence intervals for specificity and Youden's index differences excluded zero only in Dataset B, without adjustment for multiple comparisons. Paired comparisons of the area under the curve (AUC) did not establish improved discrimination. Mixup yielded the highest mean specificity and AUC, whereas Combined yielded higher mean sensitivity than Mixup. This trade-off varied across partition subsets. Cross-site and leave-one-session-out evaluations showed performance variability across acquisition settings, with no consistently best condition. These comparisons identify configuration-dependent trade-offs requiring further evaluation for diagnostic support.

title: From Silver Stains to Deep Learning: Neurohistological Analysis and Digital Mapping of the Brain of Domestic and Laboratory Animals in Veterinary Neuroscience.
abstract: Neurohistological analysis has evolved from descriptive microscopy and classical staining toward quantitative, standardized, and increasingly automated approaches. This narrative review traces this evolution in domestic animals, such as dogs, cats, horses, cattle, pigs, sheep, and goats, with humans and common laboratory animals as methodological comparators, based on the literature retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Gross dissection, selective staining, immunohistochemistry, and neuronal tracing progressively expanded the structural and neurochemical information obtainable from the brain, while macroscopic and microscopic morphometry, including design-based stereology, enabled unbiased estimation of brain volumes and cell numbers. Digital microscopy made histological slides computable, and machine learning and deep learning now allow automated segmentation directly from raw images, while magnetic resonance imaging and spatial transcriptomics link histology to connectivity and gene expression. However, direct evidence in domestic animals remains restricted to a few species and brain regions: annotated collections are scarce, data are poorly integrated, and most tools are calibrated on human, mouse, or rat brains. Open resources such as the CytoDArk0 dataset and the CISCA segmentation method are early steps forward. Progress will require species-specific brain atlases, shared protocols, and validated, interpretable methods that treat anatomical differences between species as biological information rather than noise.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Survey of Modalities, Frameworks, and Clinical Tasks.
abstract: The diagnosis of colorectal cancer encompasses nine complementary modalities: stool-based screening, blood-based biomarkers, cross-sectional imaging, endoscopic evaluation, histopathology, liquid biopsy, molecular and genetic profiling, microbiome analysis, and nanotechnology-based diagnostics. This narrative review synthesizes 160 references spanning seven task-specific artificial intelligence domains, including computer-aided detection, optical diagnosis, invasion depth prediction, computational pathology and radiogenomics, metastasis forecasting, neoadjuvant treatment response prediction, and surgical workflow analysis. We propose a conceptual multimodal pipeline comprising data ingestion, preprocessing and harmonization, feature representation, multimodal fusion, forecasting, explainability, and validation. A structured evidence grading framework classifies each clinical task by evidence level, consistency, and clinical readiness. We further catalog public datasets, challenge benchmarks, and five reporting standards: TRIPOD-AI, CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, DECIDE-AI, and CLAIM. Computer-aided detection and optical diagnosis demonstrate the highest maturity with Level 1 evidence from randomized controlled trials, while computational pathology, radiogenomics, and metastasis prediction remain at Level 2 with retrospective validation (internal or external). Microbiome screening, nanotechnology diagnostics, and surgical phase recognition are exploratory. The principal barriers to clinical adoption are domain shift, data scarcity, calibration, prospective validation, and workflow integration. We conclude that clinically useful artificial intelligence requires robust external validation, uncertainty quantification, explainable outputs, standardized reporting, and a structured translational pathway from retrospective evidence through regulatory clearance to post-deployment monitoring.

title: PET/MRI in Oncology: Real-World Recommendations.
abstract: Positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance imaging (PET/MRI) has represented a paradigm shift in medical imaging, and although its use has not yet been fully incorporated into all clinical guidelines, scientific evidence supports its ability to provide a highly accurate simultaneous metabolic and anatomical assessment, which is particularly useful for staging, treatment planning, and evaluating treatment response in cancer patients. The limited availability of the technique and the demands it places on resources and coordination suggest that its initial use should focus on those applications that can provide the greatest benefit to patients, especially within the indications related to oncological processes, where PET and MRI have a defined and complementary role. This review focuses specifically on some of these conditions.

title: Explainable DSC Perfusion Radiomics for Post-Treatment Glioblastoma Assessment Using a Soft-Voting Machine-Learning Ensemble.
abstract: Background/objectives After chemoradiation for glioblastoma, residual or recurrent tumor (tumor-positive disease, TP) and treatment-related change (TRC), which includes pseudoprogression and radiation necrosis, look alike on conventional MRI. We tested whether radiomic features from dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) perfusion MRI alone can separate them. Methods We analyzed 224 post-treatment MRI examinations from 168 patients in the public UCSD-PTGBM collection. A machine-learning ensemble was trained on 1223 radiomic features from the leakage-corrected relative cerebral blood volume (rCBV) map, with training (109 patients, 143 examinations) and test (59 patients, 81 examinations) data separated at the patient level and the model fixed before testing. The analysis was repeated on the cerebral blood flow (CBF) map from the same scans, and DSC was compared with arterial spin labeling (ASL) in patients who had both. Results On the independent test set (patient-level analysis), the model distinguished TP from TRC with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.79 (95% CI 0.67-0.89). It detected 31 of 49 patients with tumor (sensitivity 63%) and correctly identified all 10 patients with TRC (specificity 100%); at a predefined higher-sensitivity cut-off, sensitivity was 69% and specificity 80%. With the CBF map, the AUC did not differ significantly (0.78; p = 0.89), but there was a different balance of sensitivity and specificity. In an exploratory subset of 36 patients, DSC and ASL did not differ significantly (AUC 0.82 vs. 0.71; p = 0.52). Conclusions DSC perfusion radiomics alone identified tumor with high specificity but missed about one-third of tumors: a positive result may support a diagnosis of tumor, whereas a negative result cannot exclude it. External, multicenter validation is needed before clinical use.

title: Vascular and Circulating Blood Exposure to Proton or Photon Irradiation: Differentials in Lymphocyte Subset Metrics in Cancer Patients.
abstract: Background/objectives Radiation-induced lymphopenia is consistently associated with adverse outcomes across solid tumours, yet the vascular compartment that carries the irradiated lymphocyte pool is not routinely delineated during treatment planning. The VASA project makes blood vessels an explicit, measurable structure in that process. Phase II aimed primarily to establish the feasibility of that delineation and secondarily to explore how dose-volume metrics computed on MRI-segmented vessels relate to serial immunophenotyping in patients treated with protons or photons. Methods Thirty-nine patients treated between March 2021 and May 2022 were studied prospectively (30 proton, 9 photon). Flow-contrast three-dimensional MRI with three velocity-encoding directions was added to simulation; vessel masks segmented semi-automatically from the sum-of-magnitude reconstruction were imported into the treatment-planning system to generate dose-volume histograms. The effective dose to circulating immune cells (EDIC), the integral dose to vessels (IDVe) and the integral dose to target were computed. Blood was sampled at the start and at the end of irradiation for lymphocyte counts and B, T and NK immunophenotyping. Groups were compared with Welch's t -test for continuous variables and Fisher's exact test for categorical variables, without correction for multiple comparisons; the photon subgroup was not matched. Results EDIC was higher with photons than protons (5.60 vs. 1.25 Gy; p = 0.005) and in patients who became lymphopenic (4.84 vs. 1.47 Gy; p = 0.027); IDVe differed in the same direction without reaching significance (3.60 vs. 0.53 Gy·L, p = 0.091; 3.08 vs. 0.67 Gy·L, p = 0.180). Background/objectives

Radiation-induced lymphopenia is consistently associated with adverse outcomes across solid tumours, yet the vascular compartment that carries the irradiated lymphocyte pool is not routinely delineated during treatment planning. Phase II aimed primarily to establish the feasibility of that delineation and secondarily to explore how dose-volume metrics computed on MRI-segmented vessels relate to serial immunophenotyping in patients treated with protons or photons.

Methods

Thirty-nine patients treated between March 2021 and May 2022 were studied prospectively (30 proton, 9 photon). Flow-contrast three-dimensional MRI with three velocity-encoding directions was added to simulation; vessel masks segmented semi-automatically from the sum-of-magnitude reconstruction were imported into the treatment-planning system to generate dose-volume histograms. The effective dose to circulating immune cells (EDIC), the integral dose to vessels (IDVe) and the integral dose to target were computed. title: Realistic Performance Estimation in Small-Cohort Deep Learning and Machine Learning: A Leakage-Controlled Codebase Applied to Meningioma Response Prediction After Gamma Knife Radiosurgery.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Deep learning may support the prediction of meningioma response after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS), but small clinical cohorts increase the risk of overfitting and unstable performance. We developed leakage-controlled code adjusted for small clinical datasets. Methods: Pretreatment contrast-enhanced T1 MRI from 190 patients was analysed using one tumour-centred axial slice per patient. Response was defined as a tumour volume decrease ≥ 30% per log 10 (months). ResNet-10t, ResNet-18, ResNet-50 and DenseNet-121 with ImageNet or RadImageNet pretraining were evaluated in three workflows: (1) frozen backbone CNN, head-only training; (2) logistic regression or naive Bayes classification of features extracted from frozen CNNs; and (3) restricted CNN fine-tuning. Five partially overlapping chronological development/test splits were assessed, with all data-dependent fitting, feature selection and model optimisation restricted to development data. Results: The smallest RadImageNet ResNet-10t CNN performed best when fine-tuned (peak AUCs 0.953 and 1.000) but showed the widest split-to-split variation (range 0.738-1.000). When RadImageNet features extracted from ResNet-10t were classified by naive Bayes and logistic regression, they reached lower median and peak AUCs but within narrower ranges. Predictive performance did not consistently depend on CNN size. Conclusions: To our knowledge, this is the first deep learning study predicting volumetric meningioma response after GKRS. We provide openly available, ready-to-use code for three major workflows in small clinical datasets, with safeguards against information leakage. The benefit of fine-tuning and of RadImageNet pretraining depended on architecture. Robust small-cohort modelling requires attention to performance consistency across chronological splits, not only to the highest AUC in a single split.

title: Metachronous Gastric Metastasis of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Mimicking Early Gastric Cancer and Detected on Esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: Background : Although extrahepatic metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is common in the lungs and bones, metachronous gastric metastasis of HCC, which is initially detected in the form of multiple small gastric polyps, is extremely rare. Case presentation: A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with HCC by abdominal computed tomography (CT), but the patient received only intermittent treatment. After 15 months, esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed multiple 0.3-0.6 cm sessile polyps in the midbody and distal body of the stomach; these findings were not documented in the report of the previous examination. Microscopically, the stomach biopsy specimen revealed tumor cells with prominent nuclear atypia arranged in trabecular and solid patterns and infiltrating the gastric mucosa. However, no signs of glandular intraepithelial neoplasia were found in the gastric mucosa. Immunohistochemically, the tumor was positive for HepPar-1 and glypican-3 and negative for SALL4, cytokeratin-7, and cytokeratin-20, consistent with the immunophenotype of the primary HCC. Therefore, the gastric polyps were diagnosed as metachronous gastric metastasis of HCC. The patient was administered sorafenib, but follow-up CT showed radiological disease progression. He died 3 months after being diagnosed with metachronous gastric metastasis of HCC. Conclusions : Based on our experience, this rare case might help clinicians and pathologists avoid misdiagnosing gastric metastasis of HCC as primary gastric adenocarcinoma with hepatoid differentiation and prevent inappropriate treatment. In patients with HCC, biopsy of newly detected gastric polyps should be considered even when they appear benign on endoscopy, to exclude metastatic involvement.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Artificial Intelligence for the Detection and Segmentation of Periapical Lesions on Cone-Beam Computed Tomography: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) improves periapical lesion detection, but its interpretation is expertise-dependent. This systematic review evaluated artificial intelligence (AI) for detecting, classifying, and segmenting periapical lesions on CBCT. Methods : PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched to 12 December 2025 (PROSPERO: CRD420251184440). Studies comparing AI with an expert- or annotation-based reference standard on human CBCT scans were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed with the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) tool, and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled with a bivariate model where complete 2 × 2 data were available, and all metrics with univariate random-effects models. Results : Eighteen studies were included (detection or classification, 16; segmentation, 6); 15 had unclear risk of bias in at least one domain, and most were retrospective and internally validated. In the bivariate model (seven studies), sensitivity was 88.2% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 77.6-94.2%) and specificity 85.1% (73.4-92.1%). Univariate pooled sensitivity was 90.9% (84.2-94.9%; 14 studies), specificity 89.7% (83.2-93.9%; 11 studies), accuracy 86.7% (78.9-92.0%; 10 studies), and F1-score 83.7% (76.4-89.1%; seven studies). The pooled lesion Dice similarity coefficient was 0.70 (0.61-0.78; six studies), indicating moderate spatial overlap with reference annotations. Heterogeneity was considerable for detection metrics (I 2 = 90-96%), prediction intervals were wide (sensitivity 48-99%), and the certainty of evidence was very low. Conclusions : AI shows promising performance for CBCT-based periapical lesion detection under research conditions, whereas segmentation overlap is moderate. Equivalence to clinicians and clinical effectiveness are not established; prospective, externally validated studies with standardized reference standards are needed.

title: FetalSegNet: Automatic Segmentation of the Fetus and Sub-Anatomical Structures in Prenatal Ultrasound Images Using Hybrid Deep Learning Models.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Automatic segmentation of fetal anatomical structures in prenatal ultrasound images is challenging because of low tissue contrast, noise caused by speckles, anatomical variability and the fact that structures are only partially visible within individual image frames. This study has developed and evaluated FetalSegNet, a multi-label deep learning framework that can simultaneously perform segmentation of the fetus and selected sub-anatomical structures, including the head, arms, legs and heart. Methods : A dataset comprising 3321 prenatal ultrasound images obtained from 217 patients was created, with pixel-level annotations generated under expert supervision. FetalSegNet was implemented using four hybrid encoder-decoder configurations that combine EfficientNetV2-M and MaxViT-S encoders with UNet++ and Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) decoders. Performance was evaluated on an unseen test set using Dice score, intersection over union (IoU), precision, recall, 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD 95 ) and average symmetric surface distance (ASSD). The presence of anatomical structures was also assessed using classification metrics, while HiResCAM was used to examine the spatial relevance of model activations. Results : Among the FetalSegNet configurations, the EfficientNetV2-M-UNet++ model achieved the highest overall segmentation performance, with a Dice (DSC) score of 0.9232, IoU of 0.8746, HD 95 of 4.23 mm, and ASSD of 1.02 mm. Class-specific results indicated better performance in segmentation for the head and fetus, whereas the leg and heart classes showed comparatively poorer and more inconsistent results. The models also achieved high F1-scores and a high level of accuracy in assessing the presence of anatomical structures. HiResCAM analyses showed that model activations were predominantly concentrated within the corresponding anatomical regions. Conclusions : FetalSegNet provides a unified, multi-label framework for simultaneously segmenting the fetus and multiple sub-anatomical structures in prenatal ultrasound images. By combining a hybrid deep-learning architecture with independent output-mask channels, comprehensive boundary-based evaluation, and activation-based interpretability analysis, the framework offers an integrated strategy for fetal anatomical segmentation. These findings support further investigation of FetalSegNet for automated and interpretable analysis of prenatal ultrasound images.

title: The Effect of the Prognostic Nutritional Index and Triglyceride-Glucose Index for Predicting Mortality in Patients with Stroke.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Stroke is an acute condition in which impaired cerebral perfusion causes focal or global neurological dysfunction. Serious complications are a major contributor to morbidity and mortality in patients with stroke. Malnutrition is common in this population, and nutritional markers, including the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), may be useful for early risk assessment of stroke-associated infections. Insulin resistance (IR) is also an emerging risk factor for stroke and has been associated with poor prognosis through various metabolic and inflammatory pathways. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index has been proposed as a reliable surrogate marker of IR. Various biochemical and clinical parameters are used to assess prognosis in patients with stroke. We investigated the prognostic value of the TyG index and PNI for mortality and early mortality, defined as death within the first 30 days, in these patients. Methods: After application of the exclusion criteria, 415 patients with stroke were included. Demographic characteristics, including age and sex, and comorbidities were reviewed. Complete blood count, biochemical parameters, C-reactive protein, blood gas measurements, and lactate levels were recorded. Brain computed tomography and diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging findings were reviewed to classify patients into ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke subgroups. Patients were grouped as survivors or nonsurvivors, and deaths within the first 30 days were classified as early mortality. PNI and TyG index values were calculated using the following formulas: PNI = 10 × serum albumin (g/dL) + 0.005 × total lymphocyte count (cells/mm 3 ); TyG index = ln [fasting triglycerides (mg/dL) × fasting blood glucose (mg/dL)/2]. Results: Of the 415 patients included, 389 (93.7%) had ischemic stroke and 26 (6.3%) had hemorrhagic stroke. The median age was 74 years (IQR, 65.0-81.0), and the sex distribution was balanced: 207 patients (49.9%) were women and 208 (50.1%) were men. The PNI was lower in nonsurvivors than in survivors in the overall stroke cohort (ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke combined; 40.86 ± 8.02 vs. 46.88 ± 6.85, p < 0.001), the ischemic stroke subgroup (41.12 ± 8.77 vs. 46.82 ± 6.83, p = 0.001), and the hemorrhagic stroke subgroup (39.79 ± 3.79 vs. 48.17 ± 7.32, p = 0.006). The PNI was also lower in patients who died within the first 30 days than in survivors in the overall cohort (41.86 ± 8.42 vs. 46.88 ± 6.85, p < 0.001), the ischemic stroke subgroup (42.46 ± 8.90 vs. 46.82 ± 6.83, p = 0.002), and the hemorrhagic stroke subgroup (38.60 ± 4.35 vs. 48.17 ± 7.32, p = 0.012). Conclusions: Biomarkers calculated using simple hematological parameters have a significant impact on mortality and early mortality in stroke patients (both ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke). When we examined the effects of these TyG and PNI markers on mortality in stroke patients in our study, we observed that the PNI had a significant impact on mortality. Although our findings suggest that the PNI independently predicts mortality or could guide risk assessment in the emergency department, we consider this an exploratory observation, as stroke severity measures-such as the NIHSS-and relevant treatment data were not included in our analyses. However, we believe that single-point TyG values do not carry sufficient significance regarding mortality; therefore, future research should take into account cumulative, repeated TyG measurements obtained during patient follow-up.

title: Photon-Counting CT in Oral and Maxillofacial Imaging: Clinical Applications, Dose Efficiency, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) is an emerging imaging technology that combines ultra-high spatial resolution, improved dose efficiency, reduced electronic noise, and intrinsic spectral imaging. These characteristics are particularly relevant to oral and maxillofacial radiology, where accurate depiction of small osseous and dental structures is often required in the presence of metallic restorations or implants. This review summarizes the technical principles of PCCT and examines its current and potential clinical applications across dental and maxillofacial imaging. Available evidence indicates that PCCT can improve visualization of fine root canal anatomy, periodontal and trabecular bone structures, peri-implant interfaces, subtle maxillofacial fractures, and complex sinonasal anatomy. Its spectral capabilities, including virtual monoenergetic imaging and material decomposition, may substantially reduce metal-related artifacts and improve tissue characterization. Early studies also suggest that PCCT can provide high diagnostic image quality at reduced radiation dose, with potential advantages in pediatric imaging and in patients requiring repeated examinations. Beyond morphology, PCCT may support quantitative applications such as bone mineral density assessment, iodine mapping, treatment planning, and the development of imaging biomarkers and artificial intelligence-based analysis. Despite these promising findings, cone-beam CT remains the preferred modality for many routine dental indications because of its accessibility, lower cost, and established clinical workflow. Current evidence for PCCT in oral and maxillofacial radiology is still limited and is largely derived from technical, experimental, and early clinical studies. Further prospective comparisons with cone-beam CT and conventional CT are needed to define task-specific diagnostic benefits, optimized protocols, radiation-dose advantages, and cost-effectiveness. PCCT is therefore best regarded as a promising complementary modality with particular value in diagnostically challenging cases that require very high spatial resolution, spectral information, or effective metal-artifact reduction. Nevertheless, most oral and maxillofacial evidence remains exploratory; improved image-quality metrics should not be equated with superior patient-level diagnostic accuracy. Direct comparisons with optimized CBCT yield heterogeneous, protocol-dependent dose and diagnostic findings. No standardized indication-specific PCCT acquisition framework currently exists for routine oral and maxillofacial imaging. Clinical implementation should therefore be conditional on demonstrable diagnostic benefit at a justified radiation dose and acceptable resource cost.

title: Circulating MicroRNAs in Lung Cancer and Pulmonary Tuberculosis: Diagnostic Potential, Shared Signatures, and Challenges in Differential Diagnosis.
abstract: The differential diagnosis of lung cancer and pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) remains challenging because the diseases share clinical manifestations and radiological features, particularly in regions with a high tuberculosis burden. This narrative review evaluates circulating microRNAs (miRNAs), primarily measured in serum, plasma and extracellular-vesicle-enriched fractions, as potential adjunctive biomarkers for this differential diagnosis. The literature search was updated through 3 October 2026. Evidence was synthesized by comparator group, biological matrix, analytical methodology and validation design, distinguishing direct lung cancer-PTB comparisons from disease-control studies and prognostic or monitoring investigations. Numerous miRNAs have been associated with either disease, but shared candidates and opposite expression directions across separate studies do not establish differential diagnostic accuracy. Findings vary with patient selection, sample processing, detection platforms, normalization and reference standards. Direct blood-based comparisons remain limited and report variable discrimination. A plasma panel comprising miR-342-3p, miR-199a-3p and miR-199b-3p differentiated PTB from lung cancer with areas under the curve of 0.911 in training and 0.886 in internal split-sample validation; validation sensitivity and specificity were 87.9% and 75.9%, respectively. Its case-control design, incomplete microbiological confirmation and absence of concomitant lung cancer-PTB assessment limit clinical interpretation. Additional pleural-fluid findings concern a separate matrix and cannot be extrapolated to blood testing. Prognostic and treatment-associated findings remain exploratory and do not establish treatment-guiding or validated monitoring utility. Circulating miRNAs should therefore be considered potential adjuncts to clinical assessment, imaging, microbiological testing and histopathology. Clinical translation requires standardized assays, independent prospective validation in clinically relevant populations, and demonstration of incremental value and clinical utility within existing diagnostic pathways. Future studies should prespecify intended use, assay procedures and diagnostic thresholds, include patients with coexisting disease, and evaluate whether testing improves clinical decisions without replacing established microbiological or tissue confirmation methods.

title: Admission Prognostic Scores and Endoscopic Findings in Relation to the Two Components of Five-Day Treatment Failure in Acute Variceal Bleeding: An Exploratory Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Five-day treatment failure after acute variceal bleeding combines failure of bleeding control and early rebleeding, which may reflect different clinical processes. We explored whether admission scores and endoscopic findings relate similarly to these components. Methods : All 303 consecutive admissions treated with band ligation at a tertiary centre during 2021-2025 were analysed. Six scores were compared using paired AUROCs and Holm adjustment. Results : Failure occurred in 31 admissions (10.2%): 15 failures of primary haemostasis and 17 rebleeds, with one admission meeting both components. Point estimates of discrimination were higher for rebleeding for all six scores (differences 0.123-0.236), but intervals were wide, and no formal between-component test was performed. No comparison among the six scores using the primary score definitions survived the Holm adjustment for the composite or either component; this does not establish equivalence. Active bleeding at endoscopy was associated with failure of primary haemostasis (odds ratio 4.52, 95% CI 1.40-14.53), whereas its association with rebleeding was uncertain (1.07, 0.40-2.90). Red wale markings showed no clear association. Conclusions : This exploratory pattern suggests that the components may capture different clinical processes, a hypothesis requiring prospective confirmation in a larger cohort. Non-standardised outcome classification, uncertain follow-up after transfer, intervening TIPS and sensitivity to recorded versus recomputed scores limit inference.

title: DUET-Net: A Deformable CNN-Transformer with Calibrated Dual Uncertainty for Brain Tumor MRI Classification.
abstract: Background: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a primary modality for brain tumor diagnosis and treatment planning, making accurate automated classification critically important. However, existing deep learning approaches face limitations in prediction reliability, generalization across imaging domains, and calibrated confidence estimation. To address these gaps, we introduce DUET-Net, a hybrid CNN-Transformer framework that integrates six complementary architectural innovations. Methods: First, a multiscale depthwise fusion (MSDF) module aggregates multi-receptive-field context from a single 2D MRI slice using parallel depthwise convolutions at three kernel sizes. Second, domain-adaptive batch normalization (DABN) with input-conditioned mixture weights maintains domain-specific statistics while sharing affine parameters, enabling sample-adaptive generalization across imaging sources. Third, an enhanced convolutional block attention module (CBAM) introduces deformable spatial offsets to adaptively attend to irregular tumor borders. Fourth, a deformable cross-scale attention (DCSA) module combines per-scale learnable spatial offsets with adaptive cross-scale weighting for geometry-aware multi-resolution fusion. Fifth, a hierarchical Vision Transformer encoder coupled with Monte Carlo dropout and a heteroscedastic aleatoric head enables dual uncertainty estimation grounded in the Kendall-Gal framework. Sixth, post-hoc temperature calibration and Grad-CAM++ provide trustworthy confidence scores and visual interpretability. Results: The proposed model achieves 99.51% accuracy on the Kaggle dataset, 95.27% on the Figshare dataset, and 99.89% on the Mendeley dataset with an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.0142. With approximately 48 M parameters and 6.66 GFLOPs, DUET-Net sustains 52.41 FPS and is the only compared method to provide calibrated uncertainty estimation. Ablation, cross-dataset, and uncertainty-formulation comparison studies further validate the reliability of the framework. Conclusions: The potential of our proposed net as a promising approach for reliable computer-assisted brain tumor classification, although further external and prospective clinical validation is necessary before deployment.

title: Multi-Reference Evaluation of Deep Learning Tumour Segmentation in Multi-Sequence Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma MRI.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Deep learning segmentation of nasopharyngeal carcinoma is usually reported as one Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) against one reference mask, although multi-sequence MRI is often delineated separately on each sequence. We aimed to quantify how far the choice of reference changes reported performance, and to compare this with the disagreement between radiologists. Methods: We analysed a public dataset of 277 patient records with separately delineated T1-weighted, T2-weighted and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI, 30 of whom were annotated by two radiologists. Tumour volumes were compared without registration. Spatial agreement was measured after rigid registration, with the loss from transferring masks between acquisition grids estimated separately. nnU-Net models were scored against every reference, including the second radiologist's, in 102 held-out patient records. Results: Without registration, the sequence effect on tumour volume was 10.9%, against a reader effect of 5.7% (ratio 1.9, 95% CI 1.40 to 2.49). After rigid registration, per-sequence references agreed at a median DSC of 0.783, against 0.898 between radiologists; in the double-annotated patient records, the paired gap narrowed only from 0.129 to 0.083 (95% CI 0.063 to 0.111) when grid transfer was matched. One fixed set of predictions scored 0.726, 0.685 and 0.673, depending only on the reference (median per-patient reference spread 0.075), and switching the reference sequence moved scores 2.7 to 3.6 times as much as switching the radiologist. Conclusions: Part of the cross-sequence difference is a difference in what each sequence makes visible rather than annotation error, so a single-reference DSC on multi-sequence data depends on a rarely stated choice. Performance should be reported against every available reference and read against measured inter-reader agreement.

title: Beyond Conventional MRI: Molecular PET, Multiparametric MRI, and PET/MRI in Glioma Management.
abstract: Despite its central clinical role, conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides an incomplete picture of the tumor biology of gliomas, which are biologically heterogeneous tumors. Molecular positron emission tomography (PET) with amino acid tracers, multiparametric MRI techniques (perfusion-, diffusion-, and spectroscopy-based sequences), and hybrid PET/MRI have each been proposed to overcome specific limitations of anatomic imaging in diagnosis, treatment planning, and posttreatment assessment. This narrative review examined the current evidence for molecular PET, multiparametric MRI, and integrated PET/MRI across the glioma care pathway. Rather than framing these modalities as competing alternatives, we argue that amino acid transport, vascularity, water diffusion, and metabolite composition capture distinct and often spatially incongruent facets of tumor biology, such that discordance between modalities may reflect the underlying tumor heterogeneity. We also summarized the guideline recommendations (RANO/EANO, EANM/SNMMI, etc.), outlined current evidence gaps, and discussed emerging directions in novel PET tracers, artificial intelligence, radiomics, and theranostics. Molecular PET and multiparametric MRI should be used as modalities complementary to conventional MRI within multidisciplinary glioma care, while the choice and sequence of examinations should be guided by the clinical question.

title: A 3D CBCT-Based Approach to Assessing Effective Radiation Penetration Depth in Intraoperative Electron Radiotherapy.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Accurate characterization of treatment geometry is essential for intraoperative electron radiotherapy (IOeRT) treatment planning. Mobile cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) enables volumetric assessment of intraoperative anatomy beyond conventional point-based measurements. This study compared clinically applied distance measurement techniques with geometric distance descriptors retrospectively extracted from comprehensive three-dimensional CBCT datasets. Methods : Ninety-six patients receiving IOeRT as a tumor-bed boost during breast-conserving surgery were included. Manual CBCT measurements (mCBCT) were compared with mean (USavg) and minimum (USmin) ultrasound measurements per patient. Comprehensive 3D distance extraction was performed in 82 CBCT datasets using an approximated thoracic-wall surface as the geometric reference. Minimum and first-quartile distances were evaluated across the complete applicator cross-section and within a 1-cm-diameter inner disk around the central beam axis. Results : The mean paired difference between mCBCT and USavg was 0.3 mm and was not statistically significant, whereas mCBCT measurements exceeded USmin by an average of 1.5 mm. In the principal comparison, the minimum CBCT-derived distance within the inner disk was 1.4 mm smaller than mCBCT. Across the complete applicator area, minimum distances were 9.1-10.7 mm smaller than the clinical measurements. The first-quartile distance across all surface points was 1.4 mm smaller than mCBCT, whereas the corresponding inner-disk difference was not statistically significant after correction. title: Imaging as a Surgical Decision System in Modern Gynecologic Oncology.
abstract: Imaging traditionally supports gynecologic oncology through diagnosis, staging, and estimation of resectability. Contemporary treatment, however, requires longitudinal decisions about which lesion matters, when local intervention is justified, and which modality is proportionate. This critical narrative review proposes imaging as a longitudinal surgical decision system integrating disease trajectory, treatment response, target selection, operative planning, and post-intervention assessment. We define imaging-target mismatch as discordance between the radiologically dominant lesion and the lesion with greatest clinical actionability, and operationalize the disease-modifying surgical window as open, uncertain, or closed across six decision domains. Serial imaging may reveal response-created opportunities, oligopersistence, oligoprogression, competing dissemination, or the need for tissue confirmation, while CT, MRI, ultrasound, and FDG PET/CT provide complementary decision-specific information. Three-dimensional reconstruction, intraoperative imaging, radiomics, and artificial intelligence may enhance planning, but require prospective external validation and should support rather than replace multidisciplinary judgment. Decision-oriented reporting should communicate the target, lesion-level trajectory, competing disease, anatomical feasibility, residual uncertainty, and the relevance of findings to the proposed intervention. Imaging should therefore guide not only what can be treated, but what should be treated, when, and for what therapeutic purpose.

title: Preoperative CT Assessment and Perioperative Decision-Making in Gallbladder Lesions: A Descriptive Pathway Analysis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Preoperative CT may not reliably distinguish gallbladder malignancy from inflammatory disease, complicating surgical planning. We examined transitions from CT impressions through operative plans, intraoperative reassessment, index procedures, and subsequent treatment. Methods: This retrospective descriptive study screened 651 consecutive patients who underwent gallbladder surgery by a single surgeon at a tertiary referral center from January 2023 to December 2025. The analytic cohort included 41 patients with indeterminate or suspicious CT impressions or malignancy on final pathology. CT categories were assigned from original radiology reports independently of operative intent and pathology. Results: CT impressions were benign in six patients, indeterminate in 11, and suspicious in 24; malignancy was confirmed in six, three, and 16, respectively. Among indeterminate cases, eight had simple cholecystectomy plans, two frozen-guided plans, and one a radical-possible plan; all three malignant cases had conditional oncologic plans. Frozen section was performed in 11 patients, identifying malignancy in nine. Of 19 extended index procedures, 18 were performed under plans allowing oncologic extension; one represented an unanticipated extension. Six patients with T1b or more advanced cancer initially underwent simple cholecystectomy; three subsequently underwent completion surgery. Conclusions: Patients with the same CT impression followed different operative and subsequent management pathways. These findings highlight the clinical importance of considering diagnostic uncertainty throughout the surgical course, from preoperative planning and intraoperative reassessment to subsequent treatment decisions informed by final pathology.

title: MRI Radiomics-Based Nomogram Integrating Skeletal Muscle Assessment for Predicting Pathologic Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Therapy in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
abstract: Background/Objectives : We aim to develop and internally evaluate a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics-based nomogram integrating clinicopathologic and skeletal muscle measures for predicting pathologic complete response (pCR) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Methods: This retrospective study included 174 patients with stage II-III TNBC receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy ( n = 94) or chemotherapy alone ( n = 80), followed by surgery. Pretreatment MRI features underwent redundancy reduction and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) selection. Six candidate models combined radiomic, clinicopathologic, and skeletal muscle predictors. Models were fitted using Firth penalized logistic regression. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples, repeating supervised feature selection, predictor selection, and final-model selection while keeping the 325 radiomic candidates fixed. Area under the curve (AUC), calibration, prediction error, and selection stability were evaluated. Results : Eighty-five patients (48.9%) achieved pCR. Seven radiomic features constituted the score. Corrected AUCs were 0.659 for the clinicopathologic model, 0.622 after adding radiomics, and 0.629 (95% CI: 0.500-0.701) for the fully integrated model (apparent AUC, 0.793). Its corrected Brier score (0.309) exceeded the constant-prevalence benchmark (approximately 0.250). Skeletal muscle density was not independently associated with pCR ( p = 0.130) and did not significantly improve AUC over the radiomics-plus-clinicopathologic model (ΔAUC = 0.009, p = 0.428). The fully integrated model was selected in 50.3% of resamples, while 99.9% of selected models contained radiomic information. Conclusions : The radiomic score showed exploratory associations with pCR, but optimism-corrected performance and model stability were limited. Skeletal muscle density did not significantly improve discrimination. External validation is required before clinical application.

title: Performance Evaluation of Deep Learning Applications in Calcaneal Fracture Diagnosis Using Separate Radiographic Views: A Comparison of CNN and Vision Transformer Architectures.
abstract: Background: Calcaneal fractures are challenging to diagnose on routine radiographs and may result in missed diagnoses. Objective: This study compares Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures for detecting calcaneal fractures separately in three standard radiographic views: Anteroposterior (AP), Harris (axial), and Lateral. Methods: A balanced retrospective dataset of 178 patients with complete three-view examinations (89 with displaced calcaneal fractures and 89 controls) was used to evaluate five deep learning models: ResNet50, InceptionV3, InceptionResNetV2, XCiT, and PiT. After image-quality screening, each view underwent an approximately 8:2 image-level training-validation split; no independent test set was used. Images were preprocessed using data augmentation and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), while Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was employed to visualize model activation. Results: InceptionV3 achieved 100% sensitivity in the AP view, while ResNet50 achieved 100% specificity in both AP and Lateral views. XCiT matched ResNet50 across all five classification metrics in the AP view and matched ResNet50 and InceptionV3 in the Lateral view. PiT achieved 100% accuracy in the Harris validation set (95% CI, 89.0-100.0%). Grad-CAM visualizations showed activation over the calcaneal region in representative fracture images. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the feasibility of deep learning for identifying displaced calcaneal fractures through separate evaluations of AP, Harris, and Lateral radiographs. The model-specific performance patterns provide a foundation for further development of AI-assisted calcaneal fracture detection and future investigation of multi-view integration.

title: AI-Supported Semiquantitative CT Characterization of COVID-19 Pneumonia Across SARS-CoV-2 Wild-Type, Alpha, and Delta Variants and Its Association with Clinical Parameters.
abstract: Objective: An AI-based software prototype for the detection of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pneumonia was evaluated regarding its potential to quantify pulmonary opacities across Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) variant groups, incorporating clinical and radiological parameters to facilitate faster diagnosis and therapy. Methods: Chest computed tomography (CT) examinations of 255 patients with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia were analyzed using an AI-supported semiquantitative CT software prototype between November 2020 and December 2021. The results were correlated with clinical and laboratory parameters. The cohort consisted of wild-type ( n = 93), Alpha ( n = 66), Beta/Gamma ( n = 3), and Delta ( n = 93). Beta/Gamma cases were excluded from subgroup comparisons due to the small number of patients. Results: The mean AI-derived COVID-19 probability was 0.84 ± 0.33. After exclusion of five technically non-evaluable measurements, global mean opacity attenuation differed significantly among the wild-type (-475.12 ± 116.47 Hounsfield Units (HU)), Alpha (-464.68 ± 114.80 HU), and Delta groups (-423.92 ± 112.56 HU; Kruskal-Wallis H(2) = 12.062, p = 0.002). The Volume of Opacity showed no significant differences between wild-type (984.64 ± 908.92 mL), Alpha (1161.17 ± 933.55 mL), and Delta (988.19 ± 866.20 mL) ( p = 0.339). The extent of pulmonary involvement (Volume of Opacity) correlated with the duration of hospital stay (r = 0.311, p < 0.001**), duration of intensive care treatment (r = 0.468, p < 0.001**), and the laboratory parameters CRP, leukocyte count, relative lymphocyte count, and AST ( p < 0.001**). It showed no significant correlation with the duration of invasive ventilation ( p > 0.05). A total of 37 (14.5%) patients died and 92 (36.1%) required intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Manual corrections of lung lobe and infiltrate boundaries were performed in 221/255 datasets and were required in all assessed datasets (221/221, 100%). Conclusions: The CT Pneumonia Analysis Prototype enabled semiquantitative assessment of pulmonary opacities across different SARS-CoV-2 variants but required radiological oversight and manual correction of the automated segmentations. Given the retrospective observational design, the findings should be interpreted in light of potential confounding and heterogeneity in CT acquisition protocols. The observed associations suggest that combining semiquantitative CT parameters with clinical and laboratory data may be of potential relevance for future prognostic models, which requires further evaluation in multivariable analyses.

title: Reproducibility Before Treatment Decision Rules: A Targeted Scoping Review of AI-Assisted Coronary Plaque Characterization.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) can quantify plaque, whose burden predicts myocardial infarction better than stenosis severity. We reviewed evidence for artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted plaque characterization. Methods: This targeted scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) used a non-exhaustive search, mainly of MEDLINE/PubMed (July 2026, supplemented in September). AI title selection (135 of 1415 titles) and author assessment of 141 records yielded 121 included records under the revised criteria. An AI re-screen of 1280 unselected records (blind second pass on 175) found 110 further eligible records after charting; two AI passes screened 3634 confirmatory records (κ 0.93). The corresponding author accepted AI recommendations after reviewing written assessments, not blind (for the 335 confirmatory records, in one instruction). Of the 543 eligible records, 236 were charted (121 + 110 + 4 + 1; full text for 121 of the 236, abstract alone for 115) and 307 mapped from abstracts only (not fully charted). Results: In symptomatic or referred patients, AI-derived plaque burden was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (a property of the measurement, not evidence that AI improves outcomes). In one comparison, AI modestly improved discrimination over manual quantification (AUC 0.82 vs. 0.78) without significant net reclassification improvement. No randomized trial of AI-based plaque analysis reporting clinical endpoints was identified in the sources searched and assessed; TRANSFORM (NCT06112418) is recruiting. Three small same-patient comparisons found systematic between-platform differences; no adequately powered comparison of major commercial platforms was identified. Abstract-level mapping of the 307 additional records identified no randomized outcome, observed decision-impact or photon-counting prognostic study. Conclusions: AI-derived plaque measures carry prognostic information in symptomatic patients, but randomized evidence that AI-guided treatment reduces myocardial infarction or cardiovascular death in asymptomatic adults, or does so better than coronary artery calcium (CAC)-guided prevention, has not been established in the sources searched and assessed. Under the modeled effects, demonstrating benefit in the lowest-burden stage would need an impractically large trial; as a design proposal, we outline a stage-enriched randomized trial. AI-assisted plaque characterization is best understood as a throughput and within-system repeatability technology; cross-platform portability is not demonstrated, and it is not a validated treatment decision rule.

title: Large Mandibular Bone Defect Reconstruction with Calcium Phosphate Cement: A Case Report.
abstract: Background: Large mandibular defects following odontogenic cyst enucleation pose reconstructive challenges because spontaneous healing is unpredictable. Calcium phosphate cements are biocompatible, osteoconductive biomaterials that may facilitate bone repair. Case Description : We describe reconstruction of an anterior mandibular defect in a 71-year-old woman following radicular cyst enucleation using injectable calcium phosphate cement. Preoperative assessment included clinical examination, panoramic radiography, cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), and pulp sensibility testing. Imaging revealed a 27 × 35 × 6 mm defect. Cement was placed in the selected portion of the defect. Histopathological examination confirmed a radicular cyst; cyst contents underwent microbiological culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Serial panoramic radiographs and final CBCT in August 2024 allowed assessment of radiopacity, trabecular architecture, and mandibular continuity. Throughout follow-up, seven adjacent teeth (FDI 43, 42, 41, 31, 33, 34, and 35) retained positive responses to cold and electric pulp testing, whereas tooth 32 remained nonresponsive and received no endodontic treatment. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, with no infection, biomaterial-related complications, or radiographic evidence of cyst recurrence. Follow-up imaging revealed diminishing radiographic contrast between the reconstructed region and surrounding bone, emergence of a trabecular-like pattern, and preserved mandibular continuity. These findings were consistent with healing and remodeling; however, imaging could not establish cement degradation or replacement by newly formed bone. Conclusions: This case demonstrates favorable clinical and radiographic outcomes following mandibular reconstruction with injectable calcium phosphate cement. Histological confirmation would be necessary to determine the extent of cement degradation and replacement by newly formed bone.
