title: Injectable Bioactive Calcium-Magnesium Phosphate Cements Enable Balanced Material Resorption and New Bone Formation.
abstract: Injectable calcium-magnesium phosphate cements (CMPC) represent promising materials for bone defect reconstruction due to their bioresorbability, osteoconductivity, and potential to release biologically active Mg 2+ ions. In this study, injectable CMPCs based on powders containing 20 and 60 mol.% Mg 2+ were developed using a sodium phosphate solution containing carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) as the cement liquid. The effects of Mg 2+ content and CMC incorporation on the physicochemical, handling, in vitro, and in vivo properties of the cements were systematically evaluated. CMC acted primarily as a rheology modifier and structuring agent, improving paste cohesion and injectability while maintaining compressive strength suitable for bone substitution. The developed cements demonstrated controlled degradation accompanied by sustained Mg 2+ release and showed no cytotoxic effects toward MG-63 cells. Biological studies demonstrated favorable cellular responses and osteogenic potential of the developed materials. Importantly, the cement containing the higher Mg 2+ concentration and CMC demonstrated the most favorable bone defect regeneration outcomes among the investigated formulations, as evidenced by the restoration of mineralized structures observed by micro-CT and the histological identification of newly formed bone tissue. These findings demonstrate that combining increased Mg 2+ content with CMC-mediated control of cement handling properties is a promising strategy for developing injectable bioactive bone substitutes.

title: Prevalence and Clinical Characteristics of Supernumerary Teeth in a Pediatric Clinical Population: A Retrospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Hyperdontia is a dental developmental anomaly frequently associated with clinical complications such as delayed eruption, diastemas, and root resorption. This retrospective observational study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and clinical characteristics of supernumerary teeth in a Portuguese pediatric clinical population. Methods : Analyzing orthopantomograms from 1992 patients across two university clinics between 2016 and 2026, demographic and clinical variables were evaluated. The inclusion criteria comprised high-quality, accessible radiographs obtained within the last 10 years from patients aged between 5 and 18 years at the time of the examination. Results : The overall prevalence of supernumerary teeth was 1.66%. The mesiodens was the most common type, exclusively maxillary, predominantly conical, and highly impacted (86.7%). A non-significant male predilection was observed. The overall mean age at diagnosis for mesiodens was 9.87 ± 3.98 years. Posterior anomalies presented negligible prevalence (≤0.4%). Conclusions : These findings show the mesiodens as the primary supernumerary tooth. The high impaction rate at diagnosis highlights the diagnostic value of panoramic radiography when clinically indicated, supporting timely identification and individualized treatment planning.

title: Longitudinal Retinal and Cervical Spinal Cord Changes in Multiple Sclerosis: Associations with Clinical, Cognitive, and Motor Measures.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a central nervous system disease that can cause severe disability. Identifying biomarkers associated with disease progression and disability is important for MS follow-up. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) parameters, measurements of cervical spinal atrophy, and cognitive and motor performance tests were evaluated along with their changes over one year to investigate their potential role in MS follow-up. Methods: This retrospective study included 79 patients with MS. OCT and cervical magnetic resonance imaging performed at 1-year intervals, along with cognitive and motor performance tests, were evaluated. Cervical mean cross-sectional area (mCSA) was used to assess spinal atrophy. Results: Over one year, cervical mCSA and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) measurements significantly decreased. Their annual changes were not significantly correlated in the Pearson analysis. The age-, sex-, and disease-duration-adjusted linear analysis likewise did not identify a statistically significant association. Conclusions: Cervical mCSA and GCIPL thickness significantly decreased over one year, but their changes were not significantly correlated. These findings suggest that cervical mCSA and GCIPL may provide complementary information on longitudinal structural changes in MS. However, because measurement reproducibility and absolute error were not quantified for the single-reader cervical measurements, the observed mCSA decrease should be interpreted cautiously, as the extent to which it reflects biological change rather than measurement variability remains uncertain. The clinical relevance of these findings requires further validation.

title: Incremental Diagnostic Yield of Fetal MRI After Targeted Neurosonography in Fetuses with Agenesis of the Corpus Callosum: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives : This study aimed to assess additional findings reported on fetal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) after targeted neurosonography in fetuses with agenesis of the corpus callosum (ACC). Methods : This retrospective cohort included 129 singleton pregnancies with complete or partial ACC evaluated at a tertiary referral center between January 2020 and January 2023. All underwent fetal MRI within 7 days of neurosonography. Incremental findings were abnormalities not identified on the preceding examination. Final isolated or non-isolated classification incorporated both modalities. Results : MRI reported at least one incremental intracranial or craniofacial finding in 42/129 fetuses (32.6%). The most frequent findings were cerebellar hypoplasia (15/129, 11.6%), vermian agenesis (11/129, 8.5%), and arachnoid cysts (9/129, 7.0%). Final classification identified 71 isolated and 58 non-isolated cases. Among 77 tested fetuses, 15 had aneuploidy; the frequency was higher in non-isolated cases (14/37 versus 1/40; p < 0.001). Conclusions : MRI provided additional anatomical information after neurosonography in approximately one-third of this referral cohort. These findings support assessment beyond confirmation of ACC, but do not establish diagnostic accuracy, improved parental decisions, or long-term prognostic benefit.

title: Multimodal Cardiac Imaging in Aortic Regurgitation: From Pathophysiology to Diagnosis and Treatment Planning.
abstract: Aortic regurgitation (AR) is a complex and often misdiagnosed valvular heart disease. It is often asymptomatic for years, making early detection critical. Once symptoms develop, left ventricular dysfunction may already be irreversible. Timely and accurate grading of AR severity can guide clinical decision-making and improve survival rates. Delayed diagnosis increases the risk of heart failure, arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is the first-line imaging modality, providing assessment of valve morphology, AR severity, left ventricular size and function, and aortic dimensions. When TTE is inconclusive or additional anatomical information is required, complementary imaging modalities provide incremental value. Transesophageal echocardiography often helps to define AR mechanism and is particularly relevant for valve repair assessment and procedural guidance. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance enables accurate quantification of regurgitant volume and fraction, detailed evaluation of ventricular remodeling, and detection of myocardial fibrosis. Cardiac computed tomography offers high-resolution characterization of the aorta and is increasingly important for surgical and transcatheter planning. In selected patients, multimodality imaging also helps evaluate prosthetic valve dysfunction and suspected infective endocarditis. This paper reviews the currently used imaging modalities and their clinical applicability, and proposes an integrated multimodality imaging approach to guide patient management in chronic AR.

title: Relic of the Past or Clinical Compass? Re-Evaluating the Diagnostic Utility of Proton Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy ( 1 H-MRS) in Encephalitis and Infectious CNS Diseases.
abstract: Neuroimaging of inflammatory and infectious CNS diseases using conventional MRI has limitations, such as the challenging differential diagnosis of visible lesions, as well as the absence of neuroimaging abnormalities despite severe symptoms. The aim of this review is to evaluate the diagnostic utility of proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy ( 1 H-MRS) as a complementary method in inflammatory conditions and CNS infections of viral, bacterial, autoimmune, parasitic, or fungal etiology. We searched the PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus databases, including studies and case reports evaluating 1 H-MRS across age groups in the acute, subacute, and chronic phases of CNS disorders. The review demonstrates that MRS can serve as a valuable, non-invasive method capable of revealing metabolic abnormalities within normal-appearing brain tissue on conventional MRI. Furthermore, 1 H-MRS detects specific metabolites-including cytosolic amino acids, acetate, and succinate in bacterial abscesses, trehalose in fungal lesions, and guanidinoacetate in tuberculomas-assisting in their differentiation from neoplastic lesions. Neurometabolite levels may correlate with clinical status, symptom severity, and cognitive deficits, while longitudinal observations enable monitoring of disease progression and treatment response. Although 1 H-MRS is limited by spectral overlap, it represents a valuable complement to conventional MRI; however, further longitudinal studies on larger patient cohorts are required.

The aim of this review is to evaluate the diagnostic utility of proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (<sup>1</sup>H-MRS) as a complementary method in inflammatory conditions and CNS infections of viral, bacterial, autoimmune, parasitic, or fungal etiology. We searched the PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus databases, including studies and case reports evaluating <sup>1</sup>H-MRS across age groups in the acute, subacute, and chronic phases of CNS disorders. The review demonstrates that MRS can serve as a valuable, non-invasive method capable of revealing metabolic abnormalities within normal-appearing brain tissue on conventional MRI. Furthermore, <sup>1</sup>H-MRS detects specific metabolites-including cytosolic amino acids, acetate, and succinate in bacterial abscesses, trehalose in fungal lesions, and guanidinoacetate in tuberculomas-assisting in their differentiation from neoplastic lesions. Neurometabolite levels may correlate with clinical status, symptom severity, and cognitive deficits, while longitudinal observations enable monitoring of disease progression and treatment response. Although <sup>1</sup>H-MRS is limited by spectral overlap, it represents a valuable complement to conventional MRI; however, further longitudinal studies on larger patient cohorts are required.

title: Low Versus High Intraoperative Intraocular Pressure During Phacoemulsification Cataract Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Objective: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing low versus high intraoperative intraocular pressure (IOP) during phacoemulsification. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science (WoS), and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 6 July 2026, followed by a supplementary manual search conducted before data extraction on 5 August 2026, to identify any additional eligible studies. RCTs comparing low-IOP versus high-IOP strategies during phacoemulsification were included. Outcomes were categorized as intraoperative, postoperative, and safety outcomes. Data were pooled as mean differences (MDs) or risk ratios (RRs) with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using random-effects models. Results: Twelve RCTs comprising 1051 eyes were included. Cumulative dissipated energy was comparable between low- and high-IOP strategies (MD -0.12, 95% CI -0.45 to 0.20; p = 0.42). No significant between-group differences were observed in endothelial cell density, best-corrected visual acuity, central corneal thickness, or postoperative IOP across the reported follow-up periods (all p > 0.05). Intraoperative pain, aspiration time, total case time, fluid usage, and safety outcomes were also comparable between groups. Low-IOP phacoemulsification was associated with a modest increase in total ultrasound time (MD 1.53 s, 95% CI 0.03 to 3.03; p = 0.047). Conclusions: Low-IOP phacoemulsification provides intraoperative, postoperative, and safety outcomes broadly comparable to high-IOP strategies. Despite a statistically significant but clinically negligible increase in ultrasound time of approximately 1.5 s in favor of low-IOP, no significant differences were observed in cumulative dissipated energy, endothelial cell density, best-corrected visual acuity, central corneal thickness, postoperative IOP, or safety outcomes. However, these findings should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of equivalence or non-inferiority between the two strategies.

title: Image-Guided TIVAP by Interventional Radiologists: A Single-Center Cohort Study Using Institutional Surgical Benchmarks.
abstract: Background/Objectives : To evaluate the resource utilization, procedural costs, procedure time, and intraprocedural outcomes of interventional radiology (IR)-guided totally implantable venous access port (TIVAP) placement and contextualize these findings using institutional surgical benchmarks. Methods : We conducted a single-center study between March 2020 and March 2024 that included 93 patients requiring TIVAP placement for chemotherapy. All ports were inserted under ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance in an angiography suite. Surgical insertions using a cephalic vein cut-down under anesthesia were used as a comparator. Data collected included number of consent forms, staffing, procedure duration, material and medication utilization, and procedural costs obtained from hospital financial records. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize outcomes. Results : IR-guided TIVAP insertion required one combined consent form and two personnel, compared with two consent forms and four personnel for the surgical workflow. The average procedural cost in the angiography suite was €168.16 versus an institutional surgical benchmark of €407.90, representing a 58.8% lower observed cost. The recorded average procedure time was 45 min for IR versus 85 min for the surgical benchmark. Material costs were comparable, except for intravenous anesthetic agents used in the operating room. No intraprocedural complications occurred among the 93 IR cases. Conclusions : IR-guided TIVAP implantation required fewer personnel and was associated with lower observed procedural costs and shorter recorded procedure times relative to institutional surgical benchmarks. The absence of a patient-level surgical comparator and long-term follow-up limits conclusions regarding comparative safety and clinical outcomes.

title: Non-Contrast Magnetic Resonance Lymphography: Technical Approach Toward Protocol Standardization.
abstract: Background: Lymphedema is a chronic condition for which accurate imaging evaluation of the lymphatic system can contribute to diagnosis, disease assessment, and treatment planning. Non-contrast magnetic resonance lymphangiography (NCMRL) is an imaging technique that enables morphological visualization of lymphatic abnormalities without contrast agent administration. This technical report aims to describe the NCMRL protocol routinely implemented at our institution, with particular emphasis on lower-extremity imaging. Methods: The institutional NCMRL workflow performed on a 3 Tesla (3T) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) system is described, including patient positioning, three-station anatomical coverage, pulse sequence selection, acquisition parameters, geometric alignment, and image post-processing using segmental and panoramic maximum intensity projection (MIP) reconstructions. Results: The report documents the acquisition and post-processing workflow and illustrates its imaging output through representative clinical images. No systematic assessment of diagnostic accuracy, quantitative image quality, or examination success rates was performed. Conclusions: This technical report provides a structured description of an existing institutional NCMRL workflow for lower-extremity imaging. The documented approach may serve as a reference for future protocol optimization and standardization, while its reproducibility and broader clinical applicability require further evaluation.

title: Beyond Morphology: Pretransplant Tumor-to-Liver FDG Uptake Ratio Predicts Hepatocellular Carcinoma Recurrence After Liver Transplantation.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Tumor size and number do not fully capture the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence after liver transplantation. We examined whether the pretransplant tumor-to-liver maximum standardized uptake value (SUV) ratio on 18 F-FDG PET/CT is associated with recurrence, and assessed the previously reported cutoff of 1.43 in an independent cohort. Methods : We retrospectively analyzed 227 adults who underwent liver transplantation for HCC between July 2004 and November 2024 and had pretransplant FDG PET/CT. The primary endpoint was time to recurrence (TTR). The SUV ratio was analyzed as a continuous, log 2 -transformed variable in Cox models adjusted for age, MELD-Na, alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), and Milan status; the 1.43 cutoff was a secondary analysis. Death without recurrence was treated as a competing event. Results : Over a median follow-up of 80 months, 43 patients developed recurrence and 86 died. Each doubling of the SUV ratio was associated with a higher recurrence rate (adjusted HR 6.68; 95% CI 3.58-12.47) and higher mortality (HR 2.79; 95% CI 1.72-4.53). The 5-year cumulative incidence of recurrence was 44.7% with a ratio >1.43 and 7.5% with a ratio ≤1.43. Only 2 of 51 non-FDG-avid tumors recurred. The ratio added prognostic information to Milan criteria and AFP (likelihood ratio χ 2 28.5; p < 0.001) and stratified risk within the Milan criteria (5-year cumulative incidence of recurrence, 26.4% vs. 5.2%). Conclusions : A high pretransplant tumor-to-liver SUV ratio was strongly associated with recurrence independently of Milan status and AFP. External validation with standardized PET protocols is needed before clinical use.

title: Use of the ORBEYE™ Exoscope for the Treatment of Presumed Postoperative Cholesteatoma of the External Auditory Canal: A Case Report.
abstract: Background/Objectives : To describe the technical feasibility of fully exoscopic management of an unusually extensive external auditory canal cholesteatoma (EACC). Methods : We report a 26-year-old man with advanced right EACC and a history of ipsilateral myringoplasty approximately 15 years previously; a postoperative origin was suspected but could not be established. Clinical, radiological, surgical, and follow-up findings are described. Results : Imaging revealed extensive erosion of the superior EAC and adjacent temporal bone with mass effect on the right temporal lobe. The ORBEYE™ 4K three-dimensional exoscope was used throughout the operation, including dissection along exposed dura and hearing-preserving reconstruction. An intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid leak occurred at the middle cranial fossa dura and was controlled during surgery, without persistent postoperative leakage. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 4. Based on the reported four-frequency pure-tone averages, the calculated air-bone gap decreased from 18.5 to 8.5 dB HL. Diffusion-weighted MRI at 18 months showed no evidence of residual or recurrent disease, and clinical examination at 24 months showed a patent, epithelialized canal. Conclusions : This case illustrates the technical feasibility of a fully exoscopic, hearing-preserving approach to complex EACC. Comparative studies are required before conclusions about superiority or generalizable safety relative to conventional visualization can be drawn.

title: Exploring Esophageal Widening in Computed Tomography Performed in Critically Ill Patients.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Early diagnosis and therapy stratification represent central factors in the management of critically ill patients, today often assisted by clinical scores, which also include laboratory testing results. The aim of this study was to further characterize computed tomography-detected abnormal esophageal widening, which we often observe in critically ill patients in our emergency department when reading CT examinations. We expect this factor to be potentially meaningful for clinical evaluation and prognosis of critically ill patients. Methods : In this retrospective observational study, critically ill patients receiving CT trauma room imaging in our hospital's emergency department were included. In the first part of the analysis, esophageal diameter at four anatomical landmarks were compared between patients who survived and those who died within 28 days in all critically ill patients presenting with AEW. In the second exploratory part of the study, the relevance of the laboratory parameters and AEW in predicting mortality were analyzed. In part three, the correlation between the 28-day mortality of all critically ill patients and the presence of esophageal widening was assessed. Results : Esophageal widening was detected in 98 of all 1683 included patient examinations. Nineteen of these patients have died (19.4%), and ten of them (52.6%) suffered primarily from a cerebrovascular event. In the group of patients with AEW, cervical AEW was more frequent among deceased patients (63.2% vs. 27.8%; p = 0.0064), and mean maximal esophageal diameter was also greater among deceased patients (19.2 vs. 16.4 mm; p = 0.0392). Multiple laboratory parameters were also found to correlate with mortality in all patients with AEW. No significant correlation of AEW alone with 28-day mortality in all critically ill patients that received ED-CT could be demonstrated in our retrospective sample. Conclusions : Esophageal widening, especially in the upper segment, was found in a substantial proportion of critically ill patients, with increased width correlating with mortality risk in the group of patients with AEW. Future studies should include much larger patient cohorts and a prospective design to evaluate if AEW might be a candidate to serve as a potential parameter of clinical scores which aim at early patient stratification.

title: Prognostic Value of Metabolic-Muscle Reserve Index in HR+/HER2- Metastatic Breast Cancer Treated with CDK4/6 Inhibitors.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Despite the established benefits of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors, survival outcomes remain heterogeneous among patients with hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) metastatic breast cancer. We developed the Metabolic-Muscle Reserve Index (MMRI), integrating tumor metabolic activity, biochemical status, and skeletal muscle quantity, and investigated its relationship with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Methods: We conducted a retrospective study involving 168 patients with HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer who were treated with CDK4/6 inhibitors. MMRI incorporated baseline PET/CT-derived maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), albumin, and CT-derived psoas volume index (PVI). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis identified an exploratory MMRI cut-off. We examined survival using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression. Results: ROC analysis identified an MMRI cut-off of 10.68 for mortality discrimination, with an AUC of 0.642 (95% CI: 0.563-0.716). Patients with MMRI > 10.68 had shorter median PFS (14.1 vs. 28.1 months; p < 0.001) and OS (29.7 months vs. not reached; p < 0.001) than those with MMRI ≤ 10.68. In multivariable Cox analysis, higher MMRI was associated with shorter PFS (HR: 1.857, 95% CI: 1.329-2.596; p = 0.0003) and OS (HR: 1.974, 95% CI: 1.368-2.846; p = 0.0003). Conclusions: Patients with higher MMRI values experienced shorter PFS and OS during CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment for HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer. Given its modest discriminative performance, these findings remain exploratory and require prospective external validation before clinical application.

title: Osteopenia Is Associated with Inferior Survival After Deceased-Donor Liver Transplantation.
abstract: Background: Alterations in body composition have been linked to both perioperative and long-term outcomes that cause orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT). Nevertheless, the potential predictive role of recipient bone mineral density (BMD) in clinical outcomes following OLT remains uncertain. In this study, we aimed to explore the role of BMD as a prognostic factor in patients undergoing OLT after brain death donation, in the context of long-term outcome. Methods: A total of 480 patients who underwent OLT during the period from 2010 to 2023 at the University Hospital RWTH Aachen were included in the retrospective analysis. Preoperative computed tomography-based segmentation was used to measure BMD at the level of the 11th thoracic vertebra. Osteopenia was defined based previously described sex-specific cutoffs. Perioperative complications were assessed by Clavien-Dindo (CD) classification and comprehensive complication index (CCI). Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and uni- and multivariable Cox regression. Results : In our cohort, osteopenia was highly prevalent (48%). Patients with osteopenia exhibited significantly inferior overall survival (log-rank p < 0.001, observed median follow-up 52 months [14-97] vs. 59 months [18-101]) and impaired graft survival (log-rank p = 0.037, observed median follow-up 50 months [13-97] vs. 52 months [14-96]). In our multivariable model, osteopenia was confirmed as an independent risk-factor for inferior overall survival (HR 1.602, 95% CI 1.113-2.306; p = 0.011) and inferior graft survival (HR 1.379, 95% CI 1.018-1.870; p = 0.038). Furthermore, patients suffering from osteopenia required more perioperative red blood cell units (8 [4-13] vs. 6 [3-10], p = 0.027). No significant differences in perioperative complications were observed between osteopenic and non-osteopenic patients. Conclusion : The presence of osteopenia may represent an easily assessable marker associated with long-term outcome in patients undergoing OLT after brain death donation, thus underlining the predictive significance of body composition in this context. Further research is warranted to validate these findings.

title: Pregabalin and α2δ Subunit Modulation: A Systematic Review of Preclinical Evidence for Intraocular Pressure Regulation and Retinal Neuroprotection.
abstract: Background: Glaucoma is a multifactorial optic neuropathy characterized by progressive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) loss, in which both intraocular pressure (IOP)-dependent and -independent mechanisms contribute to disease progression. Gabapentinoids target α2δ subunits of voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs), which regulate calcium-dependent processes relevant to both aqueous humor dynamics and retinal neuronal function. This systematic review evaluates heterogeneous evidence relevant to α2δ modulation of IOP regulation, retinal neuroprotection, and associated molecular and synaptic pathways. Methods: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library databases from inception. Studies investigating gabapentinoids or α2δ subunit modulation with outcomes related to IOP, RGC survival, or relevant molecular signaling were included. Risk of Bias (RoB) was assessed using the OHAT rating tool, and Certainty of Evidence (CoE) was rated on the GRADE four-level scale using initial confidence criteria from the OHAT approach. Due to heterogeneity in study design and outcomes, findings were synthesized narratively, with included studies divided and assessed separately within anterior segment pharmacology, anterior segment genetics, neuroprotection, and mechanistic bodies of evidence. Results: Of 1973 unique records screened, 11 studies met inclusion criteria, which were further subdivided into 15 experimental arms according to evidence type. Distinct evidence bodies were anterior segment pharmacology (5 study arms), anterior segment genetics (3 study arms), neuroprotection (4 study arms), and mechanistic (3 study arms). Across mouse and rabbit models of spontaneous ocular hypertension, topical pregabalin (PRG) consistently reduced IOP in a dose-dependent manner, with peak effects generally occurring 1.5-5 h after administration depending on strain and formulation. Plateaus in maximal IOP reduction were observed at 0.9% PRG solution in mice and 0.6-0.7% PRG microemulsion (ME) in rabbits. ME formulations of PRG consistently prolonged duration of action and increased cumulative exposure relative to non-ME PRG formulations. PRG ME achieved maximal IOP reduction comparable to that of 0.005% latanoprost solution while retaining their increased duration of action and cumulative exposure. Repeated once-daily PRG ME dosing maintained IOP-lowering responses over 21- and 60-day treatment periods. Genetic studies separately associated CACNA2D1 / Cacna2d1 with IOP-related phenotypes and primary open-angle glaucoma susceptibility, providing target-level evidence. Preclinical posterior segment studies reported retinal structural preservation or improved RGC survival with PRG, while separate studies of GBP-L demonstrated RGC-survival effects associated with K-ATP channel activity rather than established α2δ modulation. Mechanistic studies separately identified thrombospondin-2 (TSP2)-α2δ1 signaling as a mediator of injury-associated synaptic remodeling, with pharmacologic disruption attenuating synaptic protein upregulation and improving axonal integrity. RoB varied across study arms and bodies of evidence. Anterior pharmacology included five Tier II study arms, anterior genetics included two Tier I arms and one Tier II arm, and all neuroprotection and mechanistic arms were Tier II. CoE was rated moderate for both anterior pharmacology and genetics, and low for both neuroprotection and mechanistic evidence. Conclusions: The available evidence is predominantly preclinical and heterogeneous. Moderate certainty within the defined anterior segment evidence body reflects consistency of the reported preclinical effect and does not establish clinical efficacy or independent reproducibility, as the topical PRG intervention literature is concentrated within a single investigative group. The neuroprotective and mechanistic findings remain hypothesis-generating and do not establish a unified mechanism or simultaneous IOP-lowering and neuroprotective action. Independent pharmacologic replication, validation in chronic glaucomatous neurodegeneration models, and long-term topical safety evaluation are prerequisites to discussions of clinical relevance.

title: Beyond Mucosal Healing: Quantitative Transmural Phenotyping to Assess Therapeutic Response and Support Precision Treatment in Crohn's Disease-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) is a transmural disorder in which mucosal healing may coexist with persistent mural, mesenteric, or penetrating disease. Cross-sectional imaging can therefore extend assessment beyond lesion detection toward quantitative transmural phenotyping, using imaging-derived markers to characterize inflammatory activity, structural and fibrotic burden, extramural involvement, and longitudinal treatment response. This narrative review synthesizes recent evidence on intestinal ultrasound (IUS), including contrast-enhanced ultrasound and elastography, magnetic resonance enterography (MRE), computed tomography enterography (CTE), multienergy CT, radiomics, and artificial intelligence (AI). IUS and MRE currently provide the most clinically mature approaches for serial assessment through bowel wall thickness, vascularity, composite activity indices, and measures of transmural response or healing. Conventional CTE remains important for structural and penetrating complications but is primarily morphologic and semi-quantitative. Multienergy CT introduces material-specific biomarkers, particularly iodine-based measures of inflammatory activity, whereas radiomics and AI remain largely investigational. Across modalities, persistent imaging abnormalities after treatment may provide prognostic information beyond mucosal assessment, but definitions, acquisition protocols, thresholds, and validation strategies remain heterogeneous. Quantitative transmural phenotyping may complement clinical, biochemical, endoscopic, and histological assessment, but standardization, multicenter validation, and prospective imaging-guided trials are required before routine precision-management implementation.

title: Determinants of Sagittal Alignment Following First Metatarsophalangeal Arthrodesis: The Influence of Native Anatomy, Fixation Construct, and Surgeon Experience.
abstract: Background/Objectives : Optimal sagittal alignment after first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint arthrodesis is important for postoperative function, but its determinants remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the associations of fixation method, native sagittal anatomy, and surgeon case volume with postoperative alignment. Methods : A retrospective cohort study included 272 primary first MTP arthrodeses for end-stage hallux rigidus performed between 2012 and 2022. Fixation consisted of compression screws ( n = 149) or a dorsal plate with a compression screw ( n = 123). Sagittal alignment was assessed on weight-bearing radiographs using the dorsiflexion angle (DFA) and hallux ground angle (HGA); secondary parameters were the metatarsal declination angle (MDA) and hallux valgus angle (HVA). Surgeons were stratified by case volume as high (>30), medium (10-30), or low (<10 arthrodeses). Radiographic nonunion was assessed at 6 months. Group comparisons and correlation analyses evaluated associations between fixation construct, native anatomy, surgeon case volume, and postoperative alignment. Results : Plate fixation was associated with greater postoperative hallux dorsiflexion relative to both the first metatarsal (DFA: 25.4 degrees vs. 21.9 degrees, p < 0.001) and the ground plane (HGA: 6.4 degrees vs. 4.15 degrees, p < 0.001), whereas HVA was similar between groups ( p = 0.545). The plate group demonstrated a greater MDA (21.3 degrees vs. 20.5 degrees, p = 0.028), and MDA correlated positively with DFA in both fixation groups (screw: r = 0.19, p = 0.042; plate: r = 0.29, p = 0.006). Surgeon case volume was associated with postoperative sagittal alignment, with lower-volume surgeons demonstrating greater HGA values ( p = 0.002). The overall radiographic nonunion rate was 9.6%. Conclusions : Postoperative sagittal alignment was associated with native anatomy, fixation construct, and surgeon case volume. Hallux position should be individualized according to native anatomy and confirmed by functional intraoperative assessment rather than relying on implant geometry or predefined radiographic target angles alone. Level of Evidence: Level III, retrospective comparative study.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Pulmonary Hypertension: Advancements, Opportunities, and Challenges.
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disorder associated with high morbidity and mortality. Delayed diagnosis, heterogeneous disease phenotypes, and variable treatment responses remain major clinical challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising tool for improving PH management. AI-based models have demonstrated promising performance in screening, diagnosis, classification, risk stratification, and prognosis prediction using multimodal data such as electrocardiography, chest radiography, computed tomography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, echocardiography, and electronic health records. Furthermore, AI may support individualized risk assessment, treatment-response prediction, early identification of right ventricular deterioration, and longitudinal remote monitoring. Emerging technologies, including explainable AI, federated learning, large language models, and digital twins, may further advance precision medicine in PH. Despite these advances, data quality, interpretability, privacy, and clinical implementation of AI remain challenges. This review summarizes current applications, opportunities, and challenges of AI in PH and discusses future directions for AI-assisted precision healthcare.

title: Deep Learning-Based Retinal Vascular Analysis with Quantitative Metrics for Hypertensive Microvascular Damage.
abstract: Background/Objectives : The goal of this study was to determine whether deep learning (DL)-assisted retinal vascular analysis detects subclinical microvascular remodeling associated with hypertension-mediated target organ damage (TOD) in patients with absent or mild hypertensive retinopathy (HR). Methods : This prospective study included age-comparable hypertensive patients with TOD ( n = 54), hypertensive patients without TOD ( n = 54), and healthy controls ( n = 54). Color fundus photographs underwent DL-based segmentation using the Retinal Microvascular Health Assessment System, ophthalmologist quality review, and Fiji morphometric analysis. Central retinal arteriolar and venular equivalents (CRAE and CRVE), arteriovenous ratio (AVR), and arterial and venous network metrics were quantified. Results : AVR decreased progressively from 0.814 ± 0.038 in controls to 0.740 ± 0.043 in hypertensive patients without TOD and 0.655 ± 0.042 in those with TOD ( p < 0.001). CRAE and CRVE differed among groups ( p < 0.001 and p = 0.002). Arterial fractal dimension and vessel area density (VAD) declined stepwise (both p < 0.001), whereas arterial skeletonized vascular density (SVD) and diameter were primarily reduced in TOD. Venous VAD and diameter differed ( p = 0.022 and p = 0.006), but venous SVD did not ( p = 0.146). After adjustment among hypertensive participants, TOD remained associated with lower AVR, CRAE, and all arterial network metrics except tortuosity (all p < 0.001), but not with venous parameters. Conclusions : Retinal arterial alterations were associated with established extra-retinal TOD in patients with absent or mild HR. Residual cardiovascular confounding limits interpretation, and longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal relationships, predictive value, and clinical utility.

title: MRI-Based Vertebral Bone Quality Score for QCT-Defined Osteoporosis: Incremental Diagnostic Value and an Exploratory 1.5-T Threshold in a Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background: Osteoporosis is frequently underrecognized in patients undergoing lumbar magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), creating an opportunity for imaging-based case finding. Methods: This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluated the MRI-based vertebral bone quality (VBQ) score against quantitative computed tomography (QCT)-defined osteoporosis, its incremental diagnostic value beyond age and sex, and the stability of a threshold derived under a standardized 1.5-T protocol. Among 281 consecutive adults, 278 formed the primary MRI cohort and 234 with valid L1-L2 QCT measurements formed the reference-standard cohort; 51 had osteoporosis. VBQ was calculated from L1-L4 T1-weighted vertebral signal intensities normalized to L3 cerebrospinal fluid intensity. Results: Interobserver reliability was high (intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC(2,2)), 0.919; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.899-0.935). VBQ correlated inversely with QCT volumetric bone mineral density (r = -0.687; p < 0.001) and remained independently associated with osteoporosis after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted OR, 6.08; 95% CI, 2.36-15.68). Adding VBQ increased the apparent model area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.847 to 0.896 (bootstrap optimism-corrected AUCs, 0.839 and 0.887). Standalone AUCs were 0.833 for VBQ and 0.863 for fat fraction. A VBQ threshold >3.7047 yielded 74.51% sensitivity and 83.06% specificity, but bootstrap-selected thresholds varied (2.5th-97.5th percentiles, 3.409-3.851). Conclusion: VBQ may provide an adjunctive opportunistic marker on routine lumbar MRI. However, its threshold is exploratory and requires external validation; VBQ should not be used alone to exclude osteoporosis.

title: Synthesis and Application of a Chitosan-Based AM/AMPS Flocculant for the Flocculation of Kaolinite Suspensions: Experimental and Molecular Dynamics Study.
abstract: Fine kaolinite particles form stable suspensions that impede solid-liquid separation. A chitosan-based flocculant, CS-g-P(AM-AMPS), was synthesized by ultrasound-assisted graft copolymerization of acrylamide (AM) and 2-acrylamido-2-methylpropanesulfonic acid (AMPS) onto chitosan (CS). Physicochemical characterization, batch flocculation tests, and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted with the AM/AMPS copolymer P(AM-AMPS) and polyacrylamide (PAM) as reference polymers. Characterization identified amide and sulfonate groups and a rough, porous dry-state morphology. CS-g-P(AM-AMPS) achieved higher final turbidity removal and produced larger median flocs than both reference polymers under their respective selected conditions, with a maximum removal efficiency of 98.5%. Simulations showed that the grafted polymer had the most negative total polymer-surface interaction energy and the largest interfacial hydrogen-bond population. Its segment distribution combined near-surface enrichment with extension into the adjacent aqueous phase. P(AM-AMPS) produced larger median flocs than PAM but achieved lower removal, showing that aggregate size and clarification followed different rankings. These findings suggest that extensive surface contact coupled with chain extension facilitates particle bridging and floc growth. The combined results identify CS-g-P(AM-AMPS) as an effective flocculant for clarifying kaolinite-bearing water.

title: Cachexia Index and CRP-Triglyceride-Glucose Index as Prognostic Predictors in Cancer Hospitalized Patients.
abstract: Background/objectives Cancer cachexia is linked to poor oncological outcomes. The Cachexia Index (CXI) and the CRP-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI), composite markers of body composition, nutrition, and inflammation, have emerged as prognostic tools, but their value in hospitalized cancer patients remains unexplored. We evaluated their association with short- and long-term outcomes in this population. Methods This retrospective, observational study included 139 hospitalized patients with active cancer by a Nutrition Unit during 2023. Nutritional status was assessed using the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria; body composition was quantified by computed tomography (CT) imaging at L3 level. Primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality, intensive care unit (ICU) admission due to clinical deterioration, hospital readmission, and overall survival. Each index was analyzed as a continuous variable, in quartiles, by the median, and at an exploratory ROC-derived cut-off, using logistic and Cox regression. Results CXI at its ROC-derived cut-off (<9.03; AUC 0.69) was associated with in-hospital mortality (OR 3.91; 95% CI 1.22-12.52; p = 0.022) and overall survival (HR 1.75; 95% CI 1.04-2.95; p = 0.035), unlike its continuous, quartile, and median forms. CTI at its cut-off (≥6.71; AUC 0.704) remained associated with ICU admission after adjustment for surgery and age (OR 5.52; 95% CI 1.64-18.54; p = 0.006) or surgery and myosteatosis (OR 4.94; 95% CI 1.48-16.47; p = 0.009), but not with survival. Conclusions CXI and CTI show complementary, threshold-dependent prognostic value: CXI identifies in-hospital and long-term mortality risk, and CTI, more consistently than CXI, identifies ICU admission risk due to clinical deterioration. These exploratory findings need prospective, multicenter validation.

title: From Classification to Clinical Trust: 3D Deep Learning and Layer-Wise Explainability for Brain Tumor MRI.
abstract: Preoperative differentiation of glioma from meningioma on MRI is important for treatment planning but depends on expert interpretation. A 3D ResNet-34 with CBAM attention was trained on four-modality MRI from 2251 BraTS 2023 patients (1801 for four-fold cross-validation; 450 held out for testing) and achieved 96% accuracy, an AUC of 0.993, and an expected calibration error of 0.0165 on the test set. For layer-wise explanation, Grad-CAM and SmoothGrad were applied at the four residual stages, and a reconstruction decoder was added to obtain full-resolution, decoder-mediated attribution at the 4 × 4 × 4 bottleneck, where standard Grad-CAM is too coarse. Four quantitative metrics gave complementary results: the decoder-assisted attribution had the highest pointing-game accuracy (80.2%) and the lowest deletion AUC, whereas Layer 1 had the highest insertion AUC and Layer 2 the highest mean faithfulness delta, with no significant faithfulness difference among Layers 1, 2, and 4. Glioma was localized by most layers, while meningioma was localized mainly through the decoder-assisted pathway. A preliminary clinical review and a normalization analysis are also reported. The decoder offers an annotation-free way to obtain full-resolution attribution from deep layers of volumetric models.

title: Spatial Physics-Informed Neural Reconstruction for Ultrasound Travel-Time Tomography.
abstract: Ultrasound computed tomography provides speed-of-sound (SoS) images that complement conventional pulse-echo ultrasound, but estimating spatial acoustic structure from transmission data remains computationally demanding. We investigate a physics-informed learned reconstruction trained exclusively on synthetic SoS fields and Eikonal-calculated travel times. Diverse synthetic structures supply paired training data at scale, enabling learning without experimentally labeled SoS images. A supervised inverse, a latent image prior, and physics-conditioned corrections produce an image that can subsequently be refined through the Eikonal equation. Evaluation on held-out synthetic fields shows improved reconstruction relative to the supervised initial estimate, with further gains from post-inference physical refinement. Applied to ToFs extracted from an in vivo breast acquisition, the fixed learned models recover heterogeneous internal SoS structure, and refinement improves correspondence with an independent full-waveform-inversion reconstruction. Controlled analyses characterize the contributions of spatial conditioning and the dependence of reconstruction on timing, support, and numerical sampling. These findings demonstrate that synthetic structures can provide useful prior information for ultrasound travel-time reconstruction and establish the feasibility of combining rapid learned inference with image-specific physical refinement.

title: Temporal Waveform Reconstruction Algorithm for Fast Super-resolution Ultrasound Imaging.
abstract: Objective: A processing framework is introduced to address robustness and computational challenges in translating ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM), enabling fast and adaptive microvascular imaging. Impact Statement: Parameter-free filtering and accelerated localization triple processing speed provide a reliable foundation for real-time clinical super-resolution microvascular imaging. Introduction: ULM surpasses the acoustic diffraction limit to resolve microvasculature. However, its clinical adoption is hindered by parameter-sensitive filtering and computationally heavy localization and tracking. Methods: First, a parameter-free temporal waveform reconstruction filter adaptively recovers microbubble temporal signatures from raw time-series data, separating them from tissue clutter and operating 5.7 times faster than conventional filters. Second, a Gaussian fit radial symmetry method accelerates localization by adding a Gaussian similarity step to the standard local maximum radial symmetry approach, reducing processing time to one-third. Results: The workflow processes each frame in 0.0065 s, down from 0.02 s per frame, achieving a 3-fold speedup. It delivers 10-μm-scale super-resolution microvascular imaging validated on multiple public datasets. Conclusion: This efficient and adaptive framework markedly cuts ULM processing time, paving the way to real-time clinical microvascular imaging.

title: [Safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring filtered type-B transnasal specialized airway catheter in anesthesia for ambulatory gastrointestinal endoscopic surgery in obese patients].
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the clinical safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring and filtering type B transnasal specialized airway catheter (hereafter referred to as the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway) during anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy in obese patients. Methods: This randomized controlled trial enrolled 92 obese patients (body mass index≥28 kg/m²) scheduled for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy at the General Hospital of Northern Theater Command between June and December 2025. Using a random number table, we split the participants evenly into an adjustable airway group (Group R, n =46) and a standard nasal cannula group (Group C, n =46). Anesthesia was inducted and maintained with remimazolam and alfentanil. Patients in Group R were fitted with the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway for oxygen delivery and end-tidal carbon dioxide (etCO 2 ) monitoring, and Group C received supplemental oxygen through conventional nasal cannula. The primary outcome was defined as the incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [pulse oximetry saturation(SpO 2 )<90%]. Secondary outcomes were the variations in respiratory rate, heart rate and mean arterial pressure (MAP) at time points before induction (T 0 ), upon endoscope insertion (T 1 ), 5 minutes post-insertion (T 2 ), at the end of surgery (T 3 ), and 5 minutes after waking up (T 4 ). Additional secondary outcomes included arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO₂) and arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO₂) at T 2 in both groups, and partial pressure of end-tidal carbon dioxide (PetCO₂) in group R. The duration of endoscopic therapy, dosages of remimazolam and alfentanil, the frequency of hands-on airway interventions, nasal bleeding episodes, and overall physician satisfaction scores were all systematically documented. Results: The baseline demographic and clinical characteristics matched up well between the two groups (all P >0.05). The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was significantly lower in group R compared with group C [2.2%(1/46) vs 32.6%(15/46), χ 2 =14.829, P <0.001]. Patients in Group R exhibited significantly elevated SpO 2 levels at T 1 , T 2 , and T 3 (all P <0.05). At T 2 , Group R demonstrated significantly higher PaO 2 and lower PaCO 2 compared to Group C, their heart rates also stayed distinctly lower ( P <0.05). MAP remained comparable across both cohorts at every measured interval ( P >0.05). Intraoperative PetCO 2 values in Group R were consistently maintained within normative physiological parameters, accompanied by continuous and stable monitoring waveforms. Compared with Group C, Group R registered a significantly lower rate of necessity for airway interventions, shorter endoscopic procedure duration and emergence time, lower remimazolam consumption, and highter physician satisfaction (all P <0.05). Conclusions: During anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under gastrointestinal endoscopy in obese patients, the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway directly protects against hypoxemia by improving oxygen delivery and curtails carbon dioxide retention. Concurrently, accurate ventilation tracking helps maintain a highly stable hemodynamic profile, the clinical safety and efficacy of this airway device substantially surpass those of the conventional nasal cannula.

title: A Repeatable CT-Based Protocol for Nasal Cavity Volumetry and Choanal Airway Classification in Pediatric Syndromic Craniosynostosis.
abstract: Syndromic craniosynostosis (SC), such as Apert and Crouzon syndromes, causes midface hypoplasia that severely limits nasal cavity development. A computed tomography (CT)-based volumetric protocol for nasal cavity volumetry and choanal airway classification in pediatric SC patients, using landmark-based image segmentation software, is described and tested for intra-rater reproducibility. The protocol was applied to 10 SC patients (5 Apert, 5 Crouzon; 2-48 months; paired pre-/postoperative CT) and 10 reference children (60-168 months), not age-matched because CT is rarely indicated in healthy children. Intra-rater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.987 and 0.909; 95% CI 0.934-0.997 and 0.689-0.976). Preoperative nasal cavity volume was significantly lower in SC patients (median 2,063.77 mm 3 ; Q1-Q3 1,275.53-3,457.18) than in the reference group (median 35,502.13 mm 3 ; Q1-Q3 28,811.21-39,167.15) (Mann-Whitney U = 0.000, Z = -3.780, p < 0.001). Nasal cavity volume increased between the paired CT scans in nine of ten patients (Wilcoxon Z = -2.701, p = 0.007; difference in medians +1,584.25 mm 3 ; +76.8%), remaining at only 10.3% of the reference group median postoperatively. A weighted regression sensitivity analysis (log[Volume] vs log[Age], w = 1/Age; n = 10), accounting for the age disparity between cohorts, yielded an exploratory, model-based, non-normative estimate of 7,580 mm 3 at the SC median age (8.5 months), extrapolated below the reference group age range; the SC median represented 27.2% of this estimate. Preoperative volume varied descriptively by choanal category (normal, stenosis, atresia) without tracking narrowing severity, possibly reflecting global hypoplasia; small subgroups precluded inferential testing. Nasal cavity volume is an anatomical measure and does not by itself indicate functional airway obstruction. The protocol offers a standardized workflow for larger, age-matched multicenter studies.

title: Candidate Magnetic Resonance Imaging Biomarkers of Language Recovery in Post-Stroke Aphasia: A Framework for Future Acupuncture-Response Prediction.
abstract: Language recovery after post-stroke aphasia (PSA) shows substantial interindividual variability, creating a need for objective markers that can characterize recovery potential and support individualized rehabilitation. This narrative review synthesizes magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) evidence relevant to language recovery and rehabilitation response in PSA, including structural MRI, diffusion MRI, functional MRI, and multimodal imaging. Existing studies indicate that lesion characteristics, white-matter integrity, regional functional activity, functional connectivity, and dynamic network organization are associated with aphasia severity, subsequent language recovery, or response to conventional rehabilitation. Multimodal approaches integrating imaging with clinical and behavioral information may provide a more comprehensive representation of individual recovery potential. Given the growing interest in applying neuroimaging to individualized acupuncture rehabilitation for PSA, an important question is whether these recovery-related MRI features can also inform acupuncture-response prediction. However, these findings primarily concern general prognosis or conventional rehabilitation outcomes and should not be interpreted as evidence of acupuncture-specific responsiveness. Acupuncture-related neuroimaging studies have mainly characterized treatment-associated changes in brain activity and functional connectivity rather than prospectively testing whether pretreatment MRI features predict individual treatment response. Accordingly, these MRI findings are better regarded as candidate imaging features for future acupuncture-response research than as validated predictors of acupuncture-specific benefit. We therefore propose a hypothesis-driven framework in which multimodal MRI is integrated with clinical and treatment information and evaluated within prospective controlled designs to distinguish general recovery potential from additional benefit attributable to acupuncture. Rigorous model development, external validation, and prospective testing will be required before imaging-based approaches can be considered for individualized acupuncture-response stratification.

title: The Effect of Alzheimer's Disease and Diabetes on the Volume of Brain Structures.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and diabetes mellitus (DM) are increasingly prevalent chronic disorders with overlapping effects on brain structure. However, direct volumetric comparisons among patients with AD alone, DM alone, both conditions, and healthy controls remain limited. This retrospective study compared regional brain volumes in 160 adults (18-90 years) assigned equally to four groups (n = 40 each): AD+type 1 DM, AD-only, type 1 DM-only, and healthy controls. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans were analyzed using VolBrain, an automated, multiatlas, patch-based segmentation platform, on 3D T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo (MPRAGE) images acquired at 1.5 T. Regions evaluated included white and gray matter, subcortical structures, selected cortical gyri, and the ventricular system. Analyses were stratified by sex. No significant volumetric differences were observed between the AD+DM and AD-only groups. Compared with DM-only, differences were limited to the right amygdala (p = 0.004) and left thalamus (p = 0.001) in females. Relative to controls, both AD groups showed reductions in the bilateral amygdala, bilateral caudate, right thalamus, and middle temporal gyrus, together with third-ventricle enlargement (all p ≤ 0.005). The DM-only group showed fewer abnormalities. Reduced left caudate volume was the only finding consistently observed across all patient groups and both sexes (p ≤ 0.007). Overall, AD and DM showed partially overlapping regional differences in brain volume. The consistent left caudate reduction may represent a shared structural marker and warrants further prospective and longitudinal investigation in AD-DM comorbidity.

title: Percutaneous Transhepatic Cholangioscopy: Technical Evolution and Expanding Clinical Roles.
abstract: Percutaneous transhepatic cholangioscopy (PTCS) has evolved from a niche diagnostic technique into an increasingly versatile platform for managing complex biliary diseases, particularly in patients with surgically altered anatomy or failed conventional endoscopic access. Early applications were limited by suboptimal visualization, rigid instrumentation, and procedural complexity. Refinements in endoscopic design and percutaneous techniques now support direct intraductal visualization and targeted intervention through a transhepatic tract. Recent developments include digital single-operator systems, scope miniaturization, and dedicated therapeutic accessories. These advances facilitate targeted biopsy and lithotripsy, although comparative evidence for improved diagnostic accuracy, safety, or patient-centered outcomes remains limited. Relevant literature was identified through a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE search through October 17, 2026, and reference-list screening, with bibliographic verification in Crossref. This narrative review distinguishes PTCS-specific evidence from peroral and mixed-access cholangioscopy studies and summarizes representative clinical outcomes. Technical success, diagnostic yield, malignancy-discrimination accuracy, and therapeutic success are considered separately. The review also addresses collaboration with interventional radiology, access selection, staged versus single-session procedures, drainage management, and alternative treatment pathways. Existing evidence remains heterogeneous in procedural indications, outcome definitions, adverse-event reporting, and device generations. Three-dimensional reconstruction has limited comparative clinical data, whereas the cited artificial intelligence application is a peroral feasibility report without established PTCS benefit. This synthesis aims to clarify the current role of PTCS in hepatobiliary practice and identify priorities for technique standardization, safety reporting, and prospective comparative validation.

title: Host Fitness in Gastrointestinal Oncology: Beyond Tumor Biology.
abstract: Patients with gastrointestinal cancers face site-specific threats to nutritional intake, muscle function, organ reserve, and recovery. This critical narrative review examines host fitness as an organizing concept for these vulnerabilities rather than as a validated composite score. A targeted PubMed update identified publications from 2022 through September 14, 2026, using gastrointestinal cancer terms combined with prehabilitation, microbiome-immunotherapy, geriatric assessment, exercise, and digital assessment terms, while retaining relevant foundational studies. The review distinguishes guideline-supported care from prognostic associations and research-stage applications. Geriatric and nutritional assessments can guide established supportive care, whereas computed tomography-derived body composition and inflammatory indices primarily provide prognostic information. Microbiome signatures, epigenetic clocks, and integrated digital models require further validation before they can guide treatment decisions. Intervention effects vary by tumor site and treatment phase: selected prehabilitation trials demonstrate short-term benefits, although findings remain inconsistent, while long-term exercise after adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer represents a distinct evidence base. An operational assessment protocol and multidisciplinary workflow are presented to link documented impairments with existing care pathways and repeated assessment. No host-fitness threshold is proposed for treatment escalation, de-escalation, or sequencing. Prospective studies should establish incremental predictive value and patient benefit beyond existing assessments before this integrated framework is used to support precision treatment decisions.

title: Optimized Tissue Microarray for In Situ Characterization of Central Nervous System Tumors Using a Spatial Transcriptomics Platform.
abstract: We present a standardized, end-to-end development and application of a Xenium tissue microarray (TMA) to profile glioblastoma, meningioma, schwannomas, and pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). The workflow covers: (i) pathology-guided selection of representative tumor regions (including tumor core and immune-rich interfaces when available); (ii) core extraction and array design to balance patient groups and clinical timepoints within each block; (iii) TMA embedding, sectioning, and slide preparation compatible with Xenium chemistry; (iv) assay execution, imaging, transcript decoding, and cell segmentation. This high-throughput workflow is specific for generating TMAs optimized for Xenium in situ spatial transcriptomics for different central nervous system (CNS) tumor types. Spatial profiling of CNS tumors in focused studies (i.e., clinical trials) is often limited by scarce tissue, heterogeneity across tumor regions, and batch effects introduced by processing specimens across multiple runs. Building a Xenium-compatible TMA enables uniform handling of many patient samples and time points on a single slide, thereby improving cross-sample consistency while reducing reagent cost and turnaround time. We also highlight practical troubleshooting steps encountered in tumor sections, such as tissue loss and segmentation artifacts in highly cellular or necrotic regions. Representative results are summarized using key assay quality metrics to assess performance across cores, including usable tissue area, numbers of segmented cells/nuclei per core, decoded transcript yield, genes detected per cell, and the fraction of transcripts assigned to cells. This protocol yields reproducible, cell-resolved spatial gene expression maps across multiple tumor regions in parallel, enabling direct comparison of naïve and recurrent disease within a therapeutic context. This TMA approach is broadly applicable to both untreated and treated biospecimens, where standardized processing and scalable spatial profiling are essential for biomarker discovery and mechanistic insight.

title: Diagnostic Reasoning and Staged Surgery for Culture-Negative Foot Infection Molecularly Suggestive of Mycobacterium fortuitum: A Case Report.
abstract: Post-traumatic infections caused by rapidly growing nontuberculous mycobacteria can be difficult to diagnose because clinical findings are nonspecific and conventional microbiological studies may be negative. This case describes a 15-year-old previously healthy male with a non-healing left-foot wound and intermittent fever after injury with a farm tool. Targeted next-generation sequencing of soft tissue at an outside hospital suggested Mycobacterium fortuitum, with 1296 sequence reads. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a deep infectious lesion with abscess cavity formation, and radiography suggested fifth metatarsal involvement. After admission, inflammatory markers remained elevated; however, acid-fast staining, mycobacterial deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing, 42-day mycobacterial culture, and anaerobic culture were negative. Empirical combination antimicrobial therapy targeting nontuberculous mycobacteria was initiated. Because of extensive soft-tissue infection and suspected osteomyelitis, treatment was performed in stages. First-stage debridement and dead-space management were undertaken on July 2, 2025, followed by continued antimicrobial therapy. After improvement of local inflammation, second-stage surgery on November 5, 2025 removed residual metatarsal lesions and abnormal tissue. The wound was stable at discharge, and oral faropenem was continued. Long-term outcome could not be assessed because the patient was lost to follow-up. The case emphasizes integrating exposure history, imaging, intraoperative findings, molecular testing, and deep microbiological sampling when post-traumatic rapidly growing mycobacterial infection is suspected.

title: A Reproducible Two-Session Ultrasound-Guided Radiofrequency Ablation Protocol for Dialysis-Associated Secondary Hyperparathyroidism.
abstract: Secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) is a common and clinically important complication in dialysis patients, and a subset of patients remains refractory to medical therapy or is unsuitable for surgery. Ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) has emerged as a minimally invasive image-guided treatment option for selected patients with enlarged parathyroid glands. This Methods Article describes a reproducible two-session protocol for treating multiple hyperplastic parathyroid glands under real-time ultrasound guidance. The protocol includes patient selection, biochemical and ultrasound evaluation, gland numbering, staged session planning, protective hydrodissection, in-plane electrode control, moving-shot ablation, immediate endpoint assessment, inter-session reassessment, and dialysis-specific calcium monitoring. Representative results from 20 dialysis patients show that the protocol can be implemented with rapid reduction of intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) and a need for active post-ablation calcium surveillance. The article is intended to provide a detailed procedural framework for centers developing staged ultrasound-guided parathyroid RFA rather than to establish superiority over parathyroidectomy or single-session ablation.

title: PET/CT Radiomics and Clinical Features for Classifying Transcriptome-Defined Immune Subgroups in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Tumor immune phenotypes are clinically relevant in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but tissue-based assessment is invasive and vulnerable to sampling bias. This retrospective observational study evaluated whether positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) radiomic features combined with clinical variables could classify transcriptome-defined immune subgroups. Data from 184 patients were analyzed between January 2021 and December 2024 and used a computer-generated stratified 7:3 split to form a modeling cohort (n = 129) and an internal validation cohort (n = 55). Consensus clustering of transcriptomic profiles defined two immune subgroups. After reproducibility filtering, minimum redundancy maximum relevance analysis and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression retained six radiomic features. The final combined model included the radiomic score, smoking history, pathological type, and pleural adhesion. The combined model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.841 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.772-0.909) in the modeling cohort and 0.822 (95% CI = 0.712-0.932) in the validation cohort. Compared with the radiomics-only model, the AUC gain was significant in the modeling cohort (p = 0.014) but not in the validation cohort (p = 0.590). At the modeling-derived threshold of 0.502, sensitivity and specificity were 76.5% and 82.0% in the modeling cohort and 75.9% and 69.2% in the validation cohort. Calibration intercepts and slopes were approximately 0 and 1.000 in the modeling cohort and -0.229 and 1.310 in the validation cohort. These findings support an internally evaluated association between routine PET/CT phenotypes and transcriptome-defined immune subgroups, but external validation and recalibration are required before clinical use.

title: Application of Explainable Machine Learning for Individualized Risk Stratification and Surgical Optimization in Geriatric Intertrochanteric Fractures.
abstract: Mechanical failure remains a critical complication in the fixation of intertrochanteric fractures. While the Tip-Apex Distance (TAD) is a well-established prognostic metric, the independent biomechanical impact of the nail entry point remains controversial due to confounding surgical variables. This study aimed to evaluate the stability offered by a medialized entry point using interpretable machine learning. A retrospective cohort of 628 patients treated with cephalomedullary nailing was analyzed. A Random Forest model was developed using 12 clinical and radiographic variables to predict implant failure. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to disentangle confounding factors and visualize non-linear interactions between the entry-point strategy and TAD. The medialized entry point group exhibited a significantly lower failure rate compared to the standard group (25.3% vs. 44.2%; p < 0.001). The predictive model demonstrated robust performance (AUC: 0.877) on an independent testing set. Crucially, SHAP interaction analysis revealed a "buffering" effect: while risk profiles were comparable at optimal TAD levels, the medialized trajectory significantly attenuated the probability of failure when the TAD exceeded 25 mm, potentially mitigating the increased risk associated with suboptimal screw placement. The findings identify the medialized entry point as a significant independent predictor of success, increasing the biomechanical tolerance of the fixation construct. This surgical modification offers a valuable safety margin, particularly in cases where anatomical reduction or ideal screw positioning is challenging.

title: A Digital Clinician-Technician Collaborative Workflow for Complete-Arch Implant Rehabilitation in Edentulous Patients.
abstract: This case report describes a digital clinician-technician collaborative workflow for complete-arch implant rehabilitation in a 70-year-old woman with severe periodontitis and compromised dentition. The workflow integrated clinical examination, cone-beam computed tomography, intraoral and facial scanning, mandibular movement records, virtual treatment planning, guided implant placement, and computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing. Digital data sharing facilitated communication between the clinician and dental technician throughout surgical and prosthetic procedures. Following the extraction of compromised teeth, implants were placed using digitally designed surgical guides, and implant positions were recorded with scan bodies to fabricate an immediate provisional restoration. After six months, a definitive one-piece all-ceramic implant-supported prosthesis was digitally designed and fabricated. Clinical assessment demonstrated a stable prosthetic fit, acceptable occlusion, and no major complications during follow-up. This case illustrates a reproducible, digitally coordinated approach to integrating clinical and laboratory procedures in complete-arch implant rehabilitation, while acknowledging the limitations inherent in a single-patient case report and the need for further clinical validation.

title: A CT-Based Radiomic Nomogram for Predicting FAM160A1 Expression and Survival in Ovarian Cancer.
abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) has a poor prognosis due to late diagnosis and tumor heterogeneity. Noninvasive biomarkers for guiding individualized treatment remain limited. FAM160A1 has emerged as a potential prognostic gene in OC, but its expression requires tissue sampling. This study aimed to develop and validate a contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT)-based radiomic model for the non-invasive prediction of FAM160A1 expression and to evaluate its prognostic value for overall survival (OS) in patients with OC. Transcriptomic, contrast-enhanced CT, and clinicopathological data were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA). FAM160A1 expression was associated with survival in Cox regression. Radiomic features were extracted from CT images, selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold cross-validation repeated 1,000 times, and used to construct a logistic regression model. High FAM160A1 expression was significantly associated with reduced OS in univariable analysis (HR = 1.41, 95% CI: 1.09-1.81, P = 0.008); after multivariable adjustment, the point estimate was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (HR = 1.23, 95% CI: 0.94-1.60, P = 0.13). The radiomic model predicted FAM160A1 expression with areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) of 0.830 in the training set and 0.704 under internal cross-validation. A nomogram combining the radiomic score with clinical factors predicted 60-month OS with an AUC of 0.735, and DCA indicated a net benefit over treat-all and treat-none strategies only within an intermediate range of threshold probabilities. Subgroup analysis suggested that the prognostic effect of FAM160A1 was modified by age and chemotherapy. The CT-based radiomic model can predict FAM160A1 expression and survival outcomes in OC and offers a non-invasive tool to inform individualized prognosis and treatment planning, supporting the integration of radiomics into precision oncology for OC patients; confirmation in independent, prospectively collected cohorts is required before clinical use.​.

title: Single-Stage Lower Eyelid Reconstruction with Free Tarsoconjunctival Graft, Periosteal Flap, and Tripier Flap After Basal Cell Carcinoma Excision.
abstract: Basal cell carcinoma is the most common malignancy of the periocular region, and the lower eyelid is the site most frequently involved. Full-thickness excision of lower eyelid tumors that extend laterally often removes the lateral tarsus and canthal support, producing defects that cannot be closed directly. Reconstruction must then restore the posterior lamella, the anterior lamella, and lateral canthal fixation, and at least one lamella must carry its own blood supply. The goal of this protocol is to describe a single-stage reconstruction that avoids the temporary eyelid occlusion required by two-stage techniques. The tumor is excised full-thickness with a 5 mm clinical margin, and the wound edges are cauterized and released. A periosteal flap raised from the lateral orbital rim is used as a hammock for lateral fixation. A free tarsoconjunctival graft harvested from the ipsilateral upper eyelid is sutured to the remaining lower eyelid margin and to the periosteal flap with 6-0 polyglactin 910, and a lateral canthopexy is performed with 5-0 polypropylene. The anterior lamella is rebuilt with a pedicled Tripier myocutaneous flap of redundant upper eyelid skin and orbicularis oculi muscle, which provides the vascular bed for the graft, and the donor site is closed with 6-0 polypropylene. The protocol is illustrated in an 84-year-old woman with a 3-year history of a growing pigmented lesion of the left lower eyelid. Histopathology showed an ulcerated basal cell carcinoma of solid and adenoid type with tumor at the nasal surgical margin, which was managed with topical imiquimod 5%. Because the eyelid is a high-risk site, intraoperative margin control before reconstruction is advisable whenever it is available.
