title: Rapid screening of target-specific isotope labeling protocols for in situ NMR of bacterial membrane proteins
abstract: We describe an approach for the efficient development of targeted isotope labeling protocols leading to nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) structural studies of bacterial membrane proteins in intact cells and native outer membrane (OM) vesicles (OMVs). The assay relies on the bioorthogonal non-canonical amino acid tagging (BONCAT) approach for metabolic incorporation of an azide-bearing residue, followed by copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) to an alkyne-functionalized fluorescent dye. Fluorescence detection in SDS-PAGE provides a rapid way to test samples for off-target background signal from endogenous proteins, bypassing the need for intensive NMR screening experiments. Using this approach, we develop an optimized protocol that enables high-resolution NMR spectra to be obtained in situ with negligible background signal. The BONCAT approach also enables target-specific fluorescence or nano-gold labeling of proteins at the OM surface, further extending the utility of this protocol for correlative structure-activity studies of membrane proteins in situ.
authorString: Wood NA, Gopinath T, Marassi FM.

title: Traumatic microbleeds are associated with unfavorable outcome out to 1 year after mild traumatic brain injury: A TRACK-TBI Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Importance Traumatic microbleeds (TMB) are commonly observed in mild TBI (mTBI). However, questions remain regarding their long-term prognostic significance. Objective Determine whether traumatic microbleeds predict unfavorable outcome after mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) Design The prospective longitudinal observational T ransforming R esearch a nd C linical K nowledge in T raumatic B rain Injury (TRACK-TBI) study enrolled acute TBI patients presenting to Emergency Departments (ED) at 18 U.S. Level 1 trauma centers between 2/26/2014-08/08/2018. CT and MRI were evaluated using the National Institutes of Health-National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NIH-NINDS) TBI Common Data Elements. Outcome was assessed using the Glasgow Outcome Scale–Extended (GOSE-TBI) at 2 weeks and 3, 6, and 12 months post-injury. Setting 18 U.S. Level 1 trauma centers Participants 929 GCS 13-15 patients ≥17 years old (38.5 ± 16.5 years, 66% male) who underwent clinical head CT ≤24 hours and brain MRI at 2 weeks post-injury and had at least one GOSE-TBI outcome score during 1 year follow-up. Exposure(s) Acute non-penetrating head trauma Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s) Frequency and co-occurrence of CT and MR features; incomplete recovery (GOSE-TBI <8 vs. =8) and unfavorable outcome (GOSE-TBI <5 vs. ≥5) at 2 weeks and 3, 6, and 12 months Results Generalized estimating equation models showed that TMBs and/or IVH were strongly associated with unfavorable outcome (GOSE-TBI <5 vs. ≥5) at 3, 6, and 12 months post-injury, but not with incomplete recovery (GOSE-TBI <8 vs. =8). For prediction of GOSE-TBI <5 vs. ≥5, TMBs surpassed the importance of all demographic and baseline clinical predictors throughout the 1-year follow-up period. For prediction of incomplete recovery (GOSE-TBI <8 vs. =8), brain contusions, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and subdural hematoma were more important throughout the 12-month follow-up period. Conclusions and Relevance Traumatic microbleeds (TMB) are common in mTBI. The presence of ≥4 TMBs and/or IVH is strongly associated with unfavorable outcome (GOSE-TBI <5) after mTBI out to at least 1 year, even after controlling for other neuroimaging abnormalities and demographic and clinical predictors. Better understanding of the implications of TMBs for long-term functional outcome may inform rehabilitation planning. KEY POINTS Question Do traumatic microbleeds predict unfavorable outcome after mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI)? Findings In this cohort study of 929 mTBI patients, traumatic microbleeds were common; ≥4 TMBs in at least 2 distinct regions of the brain were observed in 11.3% of participants on brain MRI performed 2 weeks post-injury. TMBs were associated more strongly with intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) than with other neuroimaging findings including brain contusions, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and subdural and epidural hematomas. The presence of ≥4 TMBs on brain MRI, or any TMB or IVH on head CT, were strongly associated with unfavorable outcome (GOSE-TBI <5) out to 12 months after mTBI. Specifically, these neuroimaging findings had odds ratios (OR) of 8.3 [2.4-29.2], 7.5 [1.8-30.8], and 5.4 [1.6-18.0] for GOSE-TBI <5 vs. ≥5 at post-injury months 3, 6, and 12, respectively. These far exceeded the ORs for other predictors including other CT and MRI findings, admission GCS score (13 vs15), age, sex, years of education, history of neuropsychiatric disorder, history of prior TBI, and contemporaneous major extracranial injury. Meaning TMBs and IVH are associated with each other, and with unfavorable outcome (GOSE-TBI <5) out to at least 12 months after mild TBI. The association persists after controlling for other CT and MRI findings, socio-demographic factors, and clinical characteristics.

Importance

Traumatic microbleeds (TMB) are commonly observed in mild TBI (mTBI). However, questions remain regarding their long-term prognostic significance.

Objective

Design

The prospective longitudinal observational T ransforming R esearch a nd C linical K nowledge in T raumatic B rain Injury (TRACK-TBI) study enrolled acute TBI patients presenting to Emergency Departments (ED) at 18 U.S. Level 1 trauma centers between 2/26/2014-08/08/2018. 18 U.S. Level 1 trauma centers

Exposure(s)

Frequency and co-occurrence of CT and MR features; incomplete recovery (GOSE-TBI <8 vs. =8) and unfavorable outcome (GOSE-TBI <5 vs. ≥5) at 2 weeks and 3, 6, and 12 months
